en.title: Apple Releases Version 27.2.1 of iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and watchOS with Bug Fixes and Security Updates
en.summary: Apple has today released version 27.2.1 of iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and watchOS, bringing bug fixes and security updates, including for a vulnerability that allowed macOS command line tools to use compromised eMudhra certificates. As the 27.2.1 updates were not distributed to external testers prior to their release, we do not have any information on whether they contain any accessibility fixes for blind, deaf blind, or low vision users at the time of writing. However, as these updates appear to have been released to address a small number of specific issues, we do not expect them to contain any such fixes. Release Notes iOS 27.2.1 This update provides bug fixes and security updates for your iPhone. For information on the security content of Apple software updates, please visit: https://support.apple.com/100100 . iPadOS 27.2.1 This update provides bug fixes and security updates for your iPad. For information on the security content of Apple software updates, please visit: https://support.apple.com/100100 . macOS Golden Gate 27.2.1 This update provides bug fixes and security updates for your Mac. watchOS 27.2.1 This update provides bug fixes and security updates for your Apple Watch. For information on the security content of Apple software updates, please visit: https://support.apple.com/100100 . How to Update iOS and iPadOS 27.2.1 are available over-the-air (Settings > General > Software Update), via Finder on a Mac with macOS Catalina or later, or via iTunes on a PC or Mac with macOS Mojave or earlier. Before updating, we strongly recommend making a full and complete backup of your device (either locally or in iCloud, depending on personal preference). This will ensure that, in the unlikely event that something goes wrong during the update process, you will have a current backup on hand in case a device restore becomes necessary. Also, if updating OTA, we recommend plugging your device into a power source for the duration of the download/installation process, so as to prevent the unlikely event of your battery going dead during the update. To install macOS Golden Gate 27.2.1, choose System Settings from the Apple menu, select General in the table, click Software Update in the scroll area, and click the Update Now button to begin the update process. If other updates are available, you can click the Info button to see details about them and select specific updates to install. watchOS 27.2.1 is available over-the-air (Settings > General > Software Update) or by going to the Watch app on your iPhone and navigating to General > Software Update. To install the update, your Watch must be connected to its charger and have at least 50% battery power.

es.summary: Normal 0 false 21 false false false ES X-NONE X-NONE /* Style Definitions */ table.MsoNormalTable {mso-style-name:"Tabla normal"; mso-tstyle-rowband-size:0; mso-tstyle-colband-size:0; mso-style-noshow:yes; mso-style-priority:99; mso-style-parent:""; mso-padding-alt:0cm 5.4pt 0cm 5.4pt; mso-para-margin-top:0cm; mso-para-margin-right:0cm; mso-para-margin-bottom:8.0pt; mso-para-margin-left:0cm; line-height:107%; mso-pagination:widow-orphan; font-size:11.0pt; font-family:"Calibri",sans-serif; mso-ascii-font-family:Calibri; mso-ascii-theme-font:minor-latin; mso-hansi-font-family:Calibri; mso-hansi-theme-font:minor-latin; mso-bidi-font-family:"Times New Roman"; mso-bidi-theme-font:minor-bidi; mso-fareast-language:EN-US;} Hola gente, ¿qué tal les va? Después de bastante tiempo trabajando en un proyecto nuevo y distinto dentro de la familia TCA Software, ¡por fin llega TCA DjMix 1.0! ¿Pero qué es TCA DjMix? Si eres de los que creció viendo a algún DJ mezclar pistas con fundidos suaves y sincronizando beats al milisegundo… pues este es tu programa. Y lo mejor: está diseñado desde cero para que cualquiera pueda usarlo con lector de pantalla. Sí, lo has leído bien. TCA DjMix es la primera aplicación de DJ accesible para Windows pensada específicamente para quienes usamos NVDA, JAWS o Narrador. Pero no es solo para nosotros: cualquier persona puede usarla con teclado, con ratón o incluso con una controladora MIDI. Y esto tiene algo todavía más especial: este es el primer programa de toda la familia TCA Software que fue construido usando Inteligencia Artificial. Sí, justo como lo lees. Por primera vez en la historia de TCA Software, creamos un programa "by coding" con ayuda de IA. CARACTERÍSTICAS PRINCIPALES TCA DjMix es una aplicación de mezcla musical accesible que reúne todo lo necesario para crear tus sesiones. Estas son sus funciones clave: • Biblioteca unificada y platos independientes TCA DjMix incluye una biblioteca centralizada donde cargas tu carpeta de música, la cual se navega 100% con lector de pantalla y lista todos los archivos automáticamente (formatos compatibles: WAV, FLAC, OGG, MP3 y AIFF). Desde esa misma lista puedes cargar las pistas de manera independiente en el plato 1 o en el plato 2 usando los atajos (Alt+1 o Alt+2), controlando el volumen y la reproducción de cada plato por separado. • Sincronización automática de BPM (Beatmatch) El Beatmatch automático analiza ambas pistas y ajusta sus tempos para que se sincronicen solos. Ideal para quienes están empezando y no quieren complicarse ajustando a mano. • Crossfader accesible El crossfader permite hacer fundidos suaves entre los dos platos, tal como lo hacen los DJ profesionales. Hola gente, ¿qué tal les va?

Después de bastante tiempo trabajando en un proyecto nuevo y distinto dentro de la familia TCA Software, ¡por fin llega TCA DjMix 1.0!

Si eres de los que creció viendo a algún DJ mezclar pistas con fundidos suaves y sincronizando beats al milisegundo… pues este es tu programa. Y lo mejor: está diseñado desde cero para que cualquiera pueda usarlo con lector de pantalla.

Sí, lo has leído bien. TCA DjMix es la primera aplicación de DJ accesible para Windows pensada específicamente para quienes usamos NVDA, JAWS o Narrador. Pero no es solo para nosotros: cualquier persona puede usarla con teclado, con ratón o incluso con una controladora MIDI.

Y esto tiene algo todavía más especial: este es el primer programa de toda la familia TCA Software que fue construido usando Inteligencia Artificial. Sí, justo como lo lees. Por primera vez en la historia de TCA Software, creamos un programa "by coding" con ayuda de IA.

TCA DjMix es una aplicación de mezcla musical accesible que reúne todo lo necesario para crear tus sesiones. Estas son sus funciones clave:

• Biblioteca unificada y platos independientes

TCA DjMix incluye una biblioteca centralizada donde cargas tu carpeta de música, la cual se navega 100% con lector de pantalla y lista todos los archivos automáticamente (formatos compatibles: WAV, FLAC, OGG, MP3 y AIFF). Desde esa misma lista puedes cargar las pistas de manera independiente en el plato 1 o en el plato 2 usando los atajos (Alt+1 o Alt+2), controlando el volumen y la reproducción de cada plato por separado.

• Sincronización automática de BPM (Beatmatch)

El Beatmatch automático analiza ambas pistas y ajusta sus tempos para que se sincronicen solos. Ideal para quienes están empezando y no quieren complicarse ajustando a mano.

• Crossfader accesible

El crossfader permite hacer fundidos suaves entre los dos platos, tal como lo hacen los DJ profesionales. Se puede controlar cómodamente desde el teclado o con el ratón.

• Efectos de sonido (Samples)

Puedes agregar efectos como scratches, fades o hits con un solo atajo de teclado. Solo hay que poner los archivos WAV de efectos en la carpeta "samples" y ya están listos para sonar.

• Compatible con controladoras MIDI (funcionalidad en versión prueba).

Si tienes una controladora Pioneer DDJ-400, DDJ-SR o DDJ-SR2, TCA DjMix la detecta automáticamente. No hace falta configurar nada: conéctala y empieza a mezclar usando los controles físicos que ya conoces.

Algunos de los atajos más prácticos para controlar todo con el teclado:

• Ctrl+L: Abrir carpeta y cargar música en la biblioteca.

• Alt+1 / Alt+2: Cargar pista seleccionada en el plato 1 o plato 2.

• F5 / F6: Reproducir o pausar el plato 1 / plato 2.

• F7 / F8: Detener el plato 1 / plato 2.

• Tab: Recorrer controles.

• Ctrl+B: Sincronizar el plato activo con el otro plato.

• Ctrl+F1 a Ctrl+F12: Reproducir samples del banco actual.

• Ctrl+S: Detener todos los samples.

• Ctrl+M: Iniciar o detener la automezcla.

• Ctrl+P: Abrir la configuración.

• Ctrl+J: Panel de controladora MIDI.

TCA DjMix está pensado para cualquier persona interesada en la mezcla musical, pero especialmente para personas ciegas o con baja visión que usan lectores de pantalla y que siempre soñaron con hacer una mezcla como un DJ profesional. Con los atajos correctos y un poco de práctica, cualquiera puede manejarlo sin necesidad de ver la pantalla.

Y hablando de práctica... ¡te lo ponemos muy fácil! Más abajo, en esta misma entrada, te dejamos el tutorial en audio y vídeo donde puedes ver y escuchar el programa en acción paso a paso.

El programa es compatible con: • Windows 10 X64.

• Windows 11.

• TCA DjMix 1.0 se distribuye como un archivo ZIP descargable. Incluye todo lo necesario: el ejecutable, los samples predeterminados y las instrucciones. No requiere instalación, simplemente descomprime y ejecuta.

• Es multilenguaje: español, italiano, inglés y portugués.

• En algunos PC, podrían necesitar la instalación de las librerías Visual Estudio C++ (en la descarga estarán).

Y lo más bonito: nació del esfuerzo dentro de la familia TCA Software, que ahora además cuenta con IA como herramienta de desarrollo. ¿Quién dice que no se puede?

es.summary: Tras una candidata a liberación, NV Access ha anunciado mediante esta publicación que ya se encuentra disponible para su descarga la versión final de NVDA 2026.3.1, el lector de pantalla gratuito y de código abierto para Microsoft Windows. Se recomienda a todos los usuarios actualizar a esta nueva versión, cuyo uso se considera apto también … Continuar leyendo "Ya disponible la versión final de NVDA 2026.3.1 con correcciones de seguridad" La entrada Ya disponible la versión final de NVDA 2026.3.1 con correcciones de seguridad se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
es.body:
Tras una candidata a liberación, NV Access ha anunciado mediante esta publicación que ya se encuentra disponible para su descarga la versión final de NVDA 2026.3.1, el lector de pantalla gratuito y de código abierto para Microsoft Windows. Se recomienda a todos los usuarios actualizar a esta nueva versión, cuyo uso se considera apto también en entornos de producción.

Esta versión contiene un parche que resuelve incidencias de seguridad. También corrige un fallo introducido en NVDA 2026.3 con el conmutador de tareas de Windows 10. Se ha restaurado la voz de Espeak NG en portugués de Brasil al comportamiento que tenía en NVDA 2026.2. Tan pronto como actualices NVDA, no olvides reiniciar el equipo. El reinicio garantiza que se pueden actualizar archivos que antes no se podían modificar porque estaban abiertos para escritura. En la práctica, al reiniciar vuelven a funcionar aplicaciones basadas en Electron, tales como Teams, Dropbox o Google Drive, y dejan de producirse comportamientos extraños con el explorador de archivos, Thunderbird, Office y algunos navegadores. Reiniciar es lo primero que debes hacer antes de informar de cualquier fallo. Hazlo pulsando windows+d para ir al escritorio, alt+f4, e intro sobre la opción Reiniciar. Puedes descargar NVDA 2026.3, así como las últimas versiones compatibles con sistemas antiguos y material útil para desarrolladores, desde nuestra página de descargas . La suma SHA256 de NVDA 2026.3.1, que se usa para garantizar la integridad de la descarga, es 6f80a5b0ca720a7d0d314b5be212f37388bbe81a1107ac3298c1821a1cd3f052. Si tienes una versión estable anterior, también puedes actualizar automáticamente desde el menú Ayuda. Y desde la rc1, con el complemento Selector del canal de actualización, se puede hacer del mismo modo configurando previamente el canal estable. Si todavía no conoces NVDA y quieres leer algo más sobre él antes de probarlo, te recomendamos consultar la guía de usuario y la referencia rápida de órdenes . Si te gustan nuestros proyectos y el contenido que ofrecemos, plantéate contribuir mensualmente con una pequeña cantidad. Tan sólo un euro es capaz de marcar la diferencia y ayudarnos a mejorar. Visita la página de donaciones para obtener más información, o la tienda para hacerte con libros de formación traducidos y sintetizadores de voz de alta calidad. ¡Feliz lunes!

La entrada Ya disponible la versión final de NVDA 2026.3.1 con correcciones de seguridad se publicó primero en NVDA en español .

en.title: Evermyth - God Life Simulator
en.summary: Become a god. Rule the world. Evermyth is a mythic life sim where you play a god from your very first prayer. Choose your domain, win the faithful, build an island realm, fall in love and face the other gods. Every life is a new myth, and every choice is yours. CHOOSE 1 OF 12 DOMAINS Death, War, Love, Sea, Sky, Nature, Knowledge, Order, Chaos, Craft, Fortune or Hearth. Each plays differently, with its own powers, prayers and stories. Be born to your seat, spring from the world itself, rise from mortal life, or seize the throne from the god before you. CREATE YOUR GOD Shape your face, hair, eyes, crown and robes in hand-drawn art inspired by ancient Greek pottery. Name your cult, choose its sacred sign, and fill a pantheon of twelve with Greek, Roman or Egyptian gods, or invent your own. WIELD 400+ DIVINE POWERS Send the rain. Hurl thunder at the assembly. Curse a king. Raise the dead. Awaken five aspects of your domain and unleash great acts: drown the world in a flood, raise a golden city, or walk among mortals in disguise. ANSWER PRAYERS, SHAPE MORTAL LIVES 400+ prayers, nearly 700 events and 240+ story chains that unfold across years. Shipwrecks, secrets, plagues, weddings, prophecies and family feuds. Every choice has a price, and mortals remember what you did. FACE CALAMITY Locust years, plague ships, great fires, a waking mountain. Save your people, bargain with another god, or let the world burn. WAGE WAR Rival realms want your island. Read your scouts and fight round by round: charge, hold the line, flank, or call down your domain to turn the battle. Sack cities, take tribute or make peace. RAISE A DIVINE BEAST Dragon, kraken, leviathan, hydra, basilisk, great wolf, golden lion, shadow panther, nine-tailed fox, star stag or moon moth. Feed it, train it, fly together, and loose it on your enemies before a hero comes hunting. LOVE, SCHEME AND FEUD Flirt, feast, beguile, trade favors and hold grudges. Marry, raise godborn children, and decide which of them deserves your seat. Win the favor of every court, from the God of the Sky to the smallest river nymph. GODS CAN FALL Rivals and even your own children can challenge you to a contest to the death. Win, and end them the old ways: cast into the pit, chained beneath a mountain, torn apart or swallowed whole. Lose, and your myth may end there. BUILD YOUR REALM Raise temples, markets, harbors, theaters and a Colossus. Keep nobles, priests and commoners on your side, or rule by fear. Change your island's climate, dress your city in your colors, and watch it come alive from dawn to night. GROW YOUR FAITH Turn a handful of believers into ten thousand faithful. Found oracles, ordain a high priest and choose the doctrines of your worship. LIVE A GOD'S OWN LIFE Wander the world as yourself, a mortal or a beast. Visit the Oracle and the Fates, take up pastimes, witness rare wonders, and earn epithets like the Merciful, Godslayer or Ender of Ages. BECOME A LEGEND Pass your seat to an heir and play on as them, or rise to the sky and set yourself among the stars. Every ended myth joins your Hall of Myths. Then begin again as a new god in a new age. PLAY YOUR WAY Free to play with no time limit. Three difficulties, from Gentle to Cruel. Day, evening and night modes. Plays offline, and no accounts, ads, subscriptions, energy timers or currencies.

en.title: Ground News
en.summary: Get all your news in one place on an eye-opening platform that shows you the bias, reliability and ownership of every source you read. Cut through the noise and escape media echo chambers with Ground News. Ground News is the largest news aggregator in the world with over 50K news sources and 60K articles added daily. But we aren’t a typical news aggregator, throwing hundreds of headlines at you that barely skim the surface. Ground frees people from algorithmic restraints, illuminates blindspots and makes media bias explicit with our one-of-a-kind media analysis features. AVOID MANIPULATIVE ALGORITHMS SPOT MEDIA BIAS DISCOVER BLINDSPOTS CHECK THE RELIABILITY OF SOURCES SEE WHO OWNS THE NEWS YOU CONSUME Read daily breaking stories from sources around the world, in real time. Like a modern day newspaper, we show you diverse stories instead of algorithm-driven content that can limit your worldview. News coverage is rarely unbiased, so we give you as much context as possible so you can come to your own conclusions. Compare coverage on partisan topics like politics, and elections. Enjoy our free features, or subscribe for in-depth analysis that will transform the way you look at news. en.title: Corner Grocer: Market Sim
en.summary: Run a little neighborhood market. Order stock, fill the shelves, set your prices, ring up customers at the register, and grow your shop from a corner store into a premium market with a second branch. Corner Grocer is a market management game built to be played with VoiceOver from the very first day. Sighted players and VoiceOver players play the same game with the same rules. A DAY AT THE MARKET • Morning: check deliveries, prices and today's event, then place your orders in the office. • Open: customers come in, ask for help and queue up. Scan their items, take cash or card, and count out the change. • Stock: open crates in the stockroom, put goods on the right shelves and watch the dates. Goods go off, and a wrong shelf sells less. • Evening: read the report, get one clear tip for tomorrow and decide what to invest in. GROW • Start with an empty corner shop and a basket of bread. Earn, then invest: shelves, fridges, freezers, produce stands, bakery cases and deli counters in build mode. • Move up through four store sizes: corner shop, mini market, big market and premium market. • License new product lines. There are 48 products, from bread and milk to hummus, pet food and olive oil. • Open extra registers and hire cashiers. Your own register is always yours. • Much later, open a second branch run by a manager you choose, and read its result in the evening report. • Invest in upgrades, supplier contracts and campaigns. Contracts and campaigns can renew themselves. • In the office, one button fills your order from the suggestions. In the stockroom, one button places every crate that has room. • Daily goals, 22 achievements, and events such as heat waves, rain, power cuts, rival sales and supplier delays. • There is no final day. Play as long as you like. BUILT FOR VOICEOVER • Every station has labelled controls in a fixed order, plus actions for the rotor. Anything you can drag also has a way to do without dragging. • Three speech levels: Full, Balanced and Sounds First. • Magic Tap pauses and resumes the day. • Sound carries information: door chimes, scanner beeps, queue alerts, shelf warnings. The Listening Room in Settings plays every sound and tells you what it means. • Easy, Normal and Custom modes, with assists for patience, day length, customer flow, wrong-shelf protection, undo and clearing spoiled goods each morning. Assists are for everyone and always free. • Short optional small jobs fill the quiet moments at the register. • Customer voices are generated with AI. You can turn them down or off in Settings. MAKE IT YOURS Decorate your shop in the Shop Studio: floors, walls, counters, signs, lights, decor and outfits, plus atmospheres, music albums and end-of-day tunes. Name your shop and let the game describe it to you. FREE TO PLAY, WITH OPTIONAL ADS AND PURCHASES The game is free to download. Cash from the shop pays for stock, shelves and upgrades. Coins are only for sound and looks; earn them by playing or with an optional ad in the Shop Studio, or buy Coin packs. Accessibility features and Easy mode are always free. ADS AND SUPPORT PACKS Ads come from Google AdMob and never play while the shop is open. From day 3 a short full-screen ad can play between days, with or without VoiceOver; the game says when an ad starts and when it closes. Once a day, an optional ad in the evening report doubles that day's profit. Support packs (Starter, Supporter, Founder) remove ads, double the evening profit without an ad and give every new shop extra starting cash. Ads are personalised only if you allow tracking. Play in 11 languages: English, Turkish, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese (Brazil), Russian and Chinese (Simplified). Customers speak all 11 languages. English and Turkish voices come with the app; the others download once while you are online. Questions or feedback: support@birkinapps.com

GROW • Start with an empty corner shop and a basket of bread. Earn, then invest: shelves, fridges, freezers, produce stands, bakery cases and deli counters in build mode. • Move up through four store sizes: corner shop, mini market, big market and premium market. • License new product lines. There are 48 products, from bread and milk to hummus, pet food and olive oil. • Open extra registers and hire cashiers. Your own register is always yours. • Much later, open a second branch run by a manager you choose, and read its result in the evening report. • Invest in upgrades, supplier contracts and campaigns. Contracts and campaigns can renew themselves. • In the office, one button fills your order from the suggestions. In the stockroom, one button places every crate that has room. • Daily goals, 22 achievements, and events such as heat waves, rain, power cuts, rival sales and supplier delays. • There is no final day. Assists are for everyone and always free. • Short optional small jobs fill the quiet moments at the register. • Customer voices are generated with AI. You can turn them down or off in Settings.

FREE TO PLAY, WITH OPTIONAL ADS AND PURCHASES The game is free to download. Cash from the shop pays for stock, shelves and upgrades. Coins are only for sound and looks, and never make the game easier or harder. You can earn Coins by playing and by watching optional ads, or buy Coin packs. Coin packs and support packs are optional in-app purchases. Accessibility features and Easy mode are always free.

ADS Ads come from Google AdMob. Optional ads in the evening report and the Shop Studio give 10 Coins each, up to 3 a day. Ads are personalised only if you allow tracking when the game asks.

Play in 11 languages: English, Turkish, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese (Brazil), Russian and Chinese (Simplified). Customers speak all 11 languages. English and Turkish voices come with the app; the others download once while you are online. Questions or feedback: [email protected]

en.title: The Day Bingo Went to Brent Cross, Met the iPhone Duo, and Bought a Pizza
en.summary: Introduction Dear old Brent Cross has featured quite heavily in my life. When I was a child, it was a brand spanking new shopping centre, famed for being absolutely enormous as well as the first attempt outside London to bring shopping and entertainment together. London had its west end, and we in north London had our north-west end in Brent Cross. My family, certain of whom have a worrying fixation with shopping trips, used to love it. Later in life, Brent Cross was where I went to get my wedding suit made. Note, dear gentleman readers, that I had my suit made, not hired, and and you should not allow yourselves to be wed in someone else's clothes either. After all, is the bride going to hire her wedding dress? Brent Cross is also where our Apple Store is, and last Saturday I persuaded Mrs Bingo to come along with me and meet the new iPhone line-up. Now, notwithstanding I've been to Brent Cross many times, I've never been on a Saturday afternoon. Don't! It's phenomenally busy and immediately put pay to the idea that I might capture a nice, atmospheric audio review of my iPhone explorations. Audio there is, but it is unfit for human consumption. Plus, although we've both been to the Apple Store there a couple of times, we had forgotten where it was. Cue a quarter of an hour wandering around past every chain store imaginable alongside coffee shops and a pop-up pizzeria, which admittedly we noted down as a place to visit on the way out, we finally remembered it was on the upper level and got there in in the end. It was the work of a moment to find a demo iPhone Duo model with which to play, safely cabled to the counter as a countermeasure to light-fingered iProdders. Let the games begin, as they say. What This Review is, and What it Ain't I want to kick off by setting some parameters. These are my unfiltered impressions. I'm not a tech journalist so I'll not be getting down and dirty with the processing power or what have you. I'm also assuming you're someone who either has the budget for the duo or who is at least very curious and perhaps wishes they had. So I'll be entirely subjective about whether it's worth the money—ultimately, that's a value judgement for each and every one of us. There may be a bit of repetition if you're familiar with other iPhone Duo pioneers' output, like the excellent Dave Nason's contributions, and if that happens it's purely coincidental, and a byproduct of my giving you my unfiltered impressions. But I have tried to keep this to a minimum and I also cross-refer to Dave's contribution, so please look at that if you haven't already. For you braillists out there, you'll be pleased to learn I did get a good go at BSI. Still reading? Thank gawd for that! A Jet-Setter's Passport Those who say the Duo is like a passport are not wrong. It really is more or less the same size and shape. I'm not talking a passport that most people have, however. I mean a passport like my mate Penguin has, because he is sent to so many foreign parts by his employer. In the UK, we have a choice of adding a good few extra pages to our passport if we're like Penguin. the Duo's like Penguin's passport, so a bit thicker than mine. Never mind Penguin, Bingo! How does it feel in the hand? Honestly? Fantastic. Size, weight, everything. I can't fault it. True, I couldn't test it in the pocket as I suspect various alarms would have gone off and I did not have a pocket at quite the right height what with its being cabled to the table and all that lark, but I could tell there'd be no trouble fitting it in any but the smallest of pockets. Dave Nason has commented on the weight. I have to say, I didn't find this at all noticeable. It is, perhaps, the weight of a wallet with a reasonable number of coins in it. That's what it feels like to hold. Not a wallet stuffed full to the seams, but a wallet with a handful of change in it. I say that on the assumption that anyone can still remember what carrying cash was like. Now, I admit I didn't hold it in my hand for very long, whereas Dave has actually been using one; but even allowing for that I was not at all concerned. Sure, it's heavier than an iPhone Air, but that's what you expect. Know When to Fold Up Dave has covered this in some detail already. For my part, I found the magnetic snap as the Duo folded very satisfying. The thing looks a very robust piece of kit when folded. When unfolded, in small tablet mode, it still feels solid—not unlike the 9.4in iPad Pro I used to own. Like Dave, I could feel the crease at the centre point but not unpleasantly so, and it does serve as a very handy orientation point. For me, and accidental though this benefit may be, I preferred it to the iPad because of this. Sound as a Pound I was in a very busy Apple Store, so bear that in mind. Additionally, the only settings I changed were to enable BSI's quick activation gesture. I played no music and listened to no books. Nevertheless, I thought Daniel compact sounded very good, both in folded and unfolded landscape modes. Indeed, the latter reminded me of the beautiful audio that I used to get from the iPad Pro. I would therefore conclude that Apple must be doing something right with this. Was it any better than the audio from the iPhone 18 Pro, which I also tried? In unfolded landscape, I would say it was, though if you're in the market for a Pro and you have a 16 Pro Max like I do, I would immediately agree that the 18 Pro is a big step up from that, and worth it for the audio alone. Braille Screen Input I had really wanted to try this and I was blown away. In unfolded Landscape, the Duo was a breeze for BSI in tabletop mode. I tried typing as fast as the cable on the table would allow in a blank note in the notes app and made hardly any errors. Those I did make were down to the unfortunate stoop I had to adopt owing to the cable on the table aforesaid, compounded by Voiceover's being set to speak both characters and words—I had forgotten how utterly tiresome I find that much keyboard echo and how it appears to slow one down. I then folded the phone and tried it in Screen Away Mode. All I can say is the speed of my Landscape tabletop typing was blasted out of the water. Again, I tried to braille as fast as I could and I can't remember making any errors. Indeed, an Apple Store employee (a South African gentleman who rather unconvincingly assured me he wasn't sneakily checking the rugby score between Italy and South Africa whenever he could) witnessed the Bingo BSI masterclass, and I found I was able to dictate what I was writing at a perfectly natural speaking pace while still managing easily to keep up using BSI. In fact, this chap, who I will later explain was the kind of Apple employee who is honest rather than only interested in sales, said I typed comfortably quicker than he had seen sighted people do on the software keyboard. But it wasn't just about speed. The Duo, particularly in its folded state, is just the right shape for BSI. I find the Pro Max begins to tire my hands after a while as I have to hold it in position to input Braille. Not so with the Duo. I can't quite describe it, but everything seemed absolutely right in terms of shape, spacing, weight and balance. It was a pleasure. I can't put it more tangibly than that. A word on calibration: it appears that dot positions are calibrated on the Duo, folded or unfolded, in the same way as they are on most iPhones. That is to say, dots 4-5-6 followed by dots 1-2-3. If you have Voiceover hints enabled, Voiceover will tell you this is how to do it. I tried the 18 Pro way just to see if it worked. It doesn't. It's definitely the traditional way. The Tent, the Laptop and the Enormous Hand A quick word on other modes available. Unfolded Portrait is what Dave describes as like having a giant iPhone. Sorry, Dave, But that doesn't go far enough. Perhaps, and it is a big perhaps, Hagrid would find unfolded Portrait useful, but I cannot think who else would. I certainly did not and will say no more about it. The other two modes are Tent Mode and Laptop Mode. In Tent Mode, the Duo is in the classic tent shape i.e. halfway between folded and unfolded. The tent roof is composed half of the titanium back of the phone (which incidentally feels exquisite to hold), and half of the outer display. Laptop mode is simply the tent turned upside down. Half the inner display rests on the table. The other half is the lid of your laptop. What are they for? I'll leave it to our South African friend now that he knows South Africa are 45-0 up at half time, to do the honours of explaining: Tent Mode is if you want to watch movies. Laptop Mode is when you want to pretend you're a novelist. I'm with Dave on this one. No use for either. But I have no sight at all, and I'd be interested to hear from someone who tries Tent Mode to watch telly in particular. Trade-Offs and Compromises As Forgive me, folks, but as our South African friend is about to feature more in our story, I do wish I'd asked the poor fellow his name. Why didn't I? Alas I have no answer to that question. Anyway we started talking about trade-offs such as no Action Button. He confirmed that he had no idea why this was and that there was no official line on it, but thought it might be possible to use the Camera Control as a quasi-Action Button by reassigning it in settings. I know this can be done on the 16 Pro Max, but I can't recall to what extent and I did not try with the Duo today. Certainly, I don't think the Camera Control can be assigned to perform functions like switching to silent mode, which you can set the Action Button to do. by the way, the Camera Control looks very similar to the Side Button on the Duo, to the extent that I tried summoning Siri with the Camera Control by mistake on one occasion. In addition, there does not appear to be any old-style mute switch on the Duo, which I thought there might be given the absence of the Action Button. Our South African friend and I also discussed the absence of the LiDAR sensor. Now, I don't use Door Detection, People Detection or Point and Speak. I've just never found I wanted to, but if you do, you won't be able to use them in the same way. As our friend explained, LiDAR gives you distances, so the Duo won't be able to do that. However, we then tried VoiceOver's Scene Recognition with both the Duo and the iPhone 18 Pro to see what extra information the phone with the LiDAR sensor would give us, both phones obviously running Visual Intelligence. My honest opinion? There was so little difference between the two descriptions as to be of no account. Even our friend was quite surprised, though he went on very honestly to say that in his view, features like Door Detection are not as good as they have been in the past. For me, these features don't matter. If they matter to you, the Duo's not your bag. Our friend was also very forthcoming on durability and battery. The battery, said he, is up with the Pro in his experience if you use it folded most of the time. unfolded, you will obviously get less. To the extent that some people say you get a lot less, well all I can say (and our friend agreed with me) is that the novelty of being able to fold and unfold our diplomatic passport of a Duo means one's likely to do it rather a lot to begin with. It's a new toy, after all. Speaking of which, I've already mentioned that the hardware seems very, very robust. This was one of the issues on which I was most sceptical and my fears have been entirely assuaged. There is always AppleCare, but even without that readers should remember that in many countries including the UK, the US, Australia and all member states of the European Union, you also have your statutory consumer rights as to fitness for purpose on which to rely. Moreover, our friend told me that AppleCare for a Duo includes replacement of the layer that might get a little worn out or creased if it becomes unpleasant under the fingers in due course. Finally, our friend confirmed what I've always suspected: whereas he himself is a Face ID fan, he's finding that more people than he bargained for like Touch ID. That's great to know for fans of the fingerprint like myself. Why can't we have both, eh? Live and let live, I say. Our friend also confirmed that the Duo is selling very well, just behind the Pro Max, at Brent Cross—an interesting observation from what is a flagship London store. So it seems sighted people are prepared to make the camera trade-offs too. I found that surprising, but gratifying now I am a Duo man. Conclusions—Why I am Sold I love iPhones, and I lov iPads. This is both. It's presented in a genuine pocket-sized form factor, is a joy with BSI, feels and sounds great, and has Touch ID, which is not only convenient but also serves as an open invitation for those who get up specially early every morning to moan about blind Touch ID obsessives to launch a fresh crusade in the comments thread! As I explored the Duo, I imagined being able to unlock my phone on the Tube without dragging the iPhone out of my trouser pocket (it wen't fit the jacket) and waving it in front of my face. I imagined watching TV with those wonderful speakers in unfolded landscape and lovely speakers, it no longer mattering if I'd forgotten the portable Bluetooth one. I imagined easier games of chess and backgammon on a tablet-like screen. I imagined breaking off reading the newspaper in Easy Reader on the right hand side to send a quick WhatsApp message on the left, before returning to the paper, with the added bonus of knowing exactly where the splitter is. I have written this whole post on my 16 Pro Max, and by comparison it's somewhat cumbersome. Sure, there are trade-offs, and I have a great deal of sympathy with the argument that if you're paying as much as you are for the Duo, you should surely not have to compromise on anything. Additionally, some compromises such as the absence of an Action Button are difficult to fathom. Nevertheless, I'll live with the trade-offs. They are far outweighed by the attractions. I hope you've found this review, for want of a better word, helpful. I'm looking forward to reading other people's observations, and I don't just mean those of the Face ID merchants. Author's note: The pizzeria mentioned in the introduction to this article has pepperoni, bacon and mushroom, and cheeseburger pizzas as meat options. They are not deep pan but are decent Italian bases. The author can attest that they are an ideal snack en route out of the shopping centre. One slice will keep you going just fine.

en.title: koedesk
en.summary: koedesk turns your iPhone keyboard into a voice-powered text input. Tap the mic, speak, tap again — your words appear instantly in any app — Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Slack, Mail, Notes, anywhere you can type. KEY FEATURES • Universal keyboard Replace the system keyboard. Works in every iOS app — chat with AI agents, draft emails, jot ideas, search the web. No copy-paste needed. • World-class accuracy Powered by ElevenLabs Scribe v2 — ranked #2 of all models on the third-party AA-WER English benchmark (2.2% WER). Accuracy measured and published across 12 languages at koedesk.app/en/benchmark/. • 36 languages, auto-detected Japanese, English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Vietnamese, and more. The keyboard reads your locale settings — no language switching needed. • Built for AI agents Optimized for natural conversation with Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini. Keyterms support lets you feed product names, codebases, and proper nouns for even higher accuracy. Filler words (um, uh) are auto-cleaned. • Custom dictionary Add specialized terms, project names, jargon — koedesk learns and adapts. en.title: Nano Empire 2
en.summary: Once, nanobots gave humans godlike power to create worlds, limited only by their imagination. But now the Creators have lost control of the creations! You, a humble starship captain, are all that stands between the galaxy and destruction. Nano Empire 2 is an incremental sandbox text adventure, featuring 30 handcrafted worlds where dreams have turned into nightmares. Endless beach parties suddenly have a leviathan problem. Crystal automata rise up against the Queen of Light. A rogue nanobot factory produces strangely beautiful horrors. A royal family of sentient trees has forgotten how to reproduce. There are also vampires, inverted merpeople, and a Great Clown Head. And of course, all these factions are at war... Without nanobots meeting everyone's needs automatically, ship captains like you are about to become the most important people in the galaxy. Transport resources to populations who desperately need them, take sides in wars or profit from both sides, befriend eccentric creatures, grow your fleet, and maybe even research a way to undo the damage. Every world has a dramatically different vision for the future of civilization, and your choices will determine which one is successful. You don't need to have played Nano Empire 1 to enjoy this game, but returning players will notice many recurring characters... -Will Peter Frederick ever grow up and care about something other than partying? -Will Zithguul the giant scorpion escape from the Petting Zoo? -What will happen with Roland, Carla, and the ongoing conflict between the Underworld and the Core?* Features: -100% human-written. No generative AI was used to make this game. -Simple and elegant resource management as in Nano Empire 1. All the storytelling of an open world space opera with none of the tedious inventory management. -30 factions playing out a dynamic simulation of economy, war, and culture. Every action you take affects the balance of power. -Several days of idle gameplay. Each world unlocks new activities over time as it grows. -Collect artifacts and allies with world-shattering effects (sometimes literally). -Over 40 possible endings! (You can experience multiple endings without having to restart the game every time. A handy Ending Tracker is included.) -Play the complete game for free with no ads. An in-app purchase is available to unlock optional worlds and bonus resources. -Fully accessible with VoiceOver. *If you haven't already figured it out, this game takes place after the most interesting ending of Nano Empire: the one with the apocalypse...

en.title: FruitPot Adventures
en.summary: A luxury hotel, a missing necklace, and a resourceful detective. Enjoy hours of fun in a free mystery adventure you can play offline, with VoiceOver support. Join James F. Pot as he investigates the Golden Lion Hotel. Talk to its quirky guests, uncover clues, try on disguises, and combine items to solve situations that are as puzzling as they are hilarious. HOURS OF FUN AND CLEVER PUZZLES Explore the hotel and tackle logic, memory, and sound puzzles. Every conversation and every item could help you move forward. Sometimes you’ll need a tool. Sometimes, a disguise. And almost always, a little ingenuity. PLAY OFFLINE, AT YOUR OWN PACE Play without an internet connection and take your investigation wherever you go. Automatic saving keeps your progress safe, and three save slots let you organize your adventures. FOR IPHONE AND IPAD Enjoy retro-style scenery, music, and memorable characters, with text in English, Spanish, French, German and Italian. THE COMPLETE GAME IS FREE No ads and no payments required to continue the story. You can finish the entire adventure for free. If you’d like to support future adventures, you’ll find four optional contribution levels under the star on the main menu. Each level unlocks a supporter emblem, without gameplay advantages or content needed to finish the adventure. Contributions require an internet connection to the App Store. es.title: Nuevo curso de introducción a Python de NVDA.es y otras actualizaciones
es.summary: ¡Hola, comunidad! Llevábamos tiempo sin traer novedades por aquí. Aprovechando que NVDA 2026.3.1 está al caer, hemos pensado que era un buen momento. En esta entrada te hablamos de la A11yconf 2026, nuestra nueva plataforma de formación y el nuevo curso que estrenamos junto a ella, y el cifrado de datos en TeleNVDA. ¡Comenzamos! A11yconf … Continuar leyendo "Nuevo curso de introducción a Python de NVDA.es y otras actualizaciones" La entrada Nuevo curso de introducción a Python de NVDA.es y otras actualizaciones se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
es.body:
¡Hola, comunidad! Llevábamos tiempo sin traer novedades por aquí. Aprovechando que NVDA 2026.3.1 está al caer, hemos pensado que era un buen momento. En esta entrada te hablamos de la A11yconf 2026, nuestra nueva plataforma de formación y el nuevo curso que estrenamos junto a ella, y el cifrado de datos en TeleNVDA. ¡Comenzamos!

La A11yconf del año pasado salió muy bien, hasta el punto de que este año han repetido. Nosotros, por nuestra parte, también hemos repetido patrocinando el evento y echando una mano para que dispongan de los recursos necesarios. Este año, la A11yconf tendrá lugar el 28 de noviembre en Zaragoza. Si todavía no tienes tu entrada, ¡te aconsejamos comprarla cuanto antes! Visita la página de la A11yconf En esta ocasión no disponemos de stand independiente, pero estaremos en el recinto. ¡No dudes en preguntar por nosotros si vas por allí!

La inteligencia artificial generativa ha venido a revolucionar nuestra forma de trabajar, sin importar el sector. Si tenemos un ordenador delante, ya es habitual hablar de Claude, Gemini o GPT. Y en el desarrollo de NVDA no podía ser menos: es raro el día que no aparece un complemento nuevo en la tienda internacional. Montones de nuevos autores construyen y comparten complementos cuyo desarrollo ha sido asistido o enteramente realizado por la IA. A priori, esto suena a cambio positivo. Sin embargo, la realidad es muy distinta. A menudo nos encontramos complementos que duplican funciones existentes de otros complementos, están plagados de fallos, o añaden funciones que ya vienen en el propio NVDA. La tienda está llena de traductores, descargadores de Youtube, reproductores de radio, y complementos para preguntar a la IA, entre otros. Muchas personas que no se conocen entre sí tienen la misma idea. La IA, que tiende cada vez más a dar el mismo resultado con las mismas condiciones de partida, elabora complementos con sutiles diferencias, que en esencia son iguales y pueden coincidir hasta en nombre. A la falta de análisis previo se unen la falta de conocimientos en programación y la ausencia de juicio crítico. Muchos de los autores que han sumado complementos a la tienda no tienen conocimientos de programación, y por tanto son incapaces de defender por sí mismos sus propias creaciones. Con este panorama, estamos seguros de que entenderás por qué sólo se actualizan complementos clásicos en el catálogo de nuestra comunidad, y por qué no añadimos complementos nuevos. Los esfuerzos necesarios para filtrar y revisar se han disparado hasta un punto que, con el escaso tiempo que tenemos, se ha vuelto inasumible. Así que hemos decidido entrar en acción utilizando exactamente la misma herramienta que causa el problema: la IA. Bien usada, la inteligencia artificial constituye una herramienta muy potente. Gracias a ella, hemos preparado un curso en el que, paradójicamente, el uso de IA está prohibido, así como el uso de entornos de desarrollo con autocompletado e indentado automático. Se trata de un curso de introducción a Python que ayuda a sentar las bases del lenguaje y enseña a obtener información de Internet y crear interfaces gráficas. Quien supere el curso será capaz de leer código fuente, ya sea de NVDA o de un complemento, y comprender lo que hará el intérprete con ese código. Como bien han podido comprobar los participantes de nuestra prueba piloto, el curso entraña cierta dificultad, y no es el típico que se saca en dos tardes: además de los conceptos teóricos, existen ejercicios prácticos, todos de respuesta abierta y corregidos a mano. Queremos que aprendas a programar en condiciones, interiorizando cada concepto. Las herramientas que uses después, ya son cosa tuya, pero tendrás la capacidad de juzgar el resultado. El acceso al curso es totalmente gratuito. Opcionalmente, al acabar, podrás comprar un certificado de aprovechamiento, en el que también contemplamos descuentos para personas que pasen por dificultades económicas. El curso funciona sobre una plataforma de formación propia, también construida con la ayuda de la IA. Puedes ver su código fuente en este repositorio y conectarte directamente a ella en la siguiente dirección: https://formacion.nvda.es . ¡Te esperamos!

En los protocolos y programas de control remoto con NVDA, la seguridad siempre ha tenido una prioridad crítica. NVDA es un lector de pantalla que capta, procesa y devuelve un montón de información que puede contener datos sensibles y jugarnos una mala pasada si cae en malas manos. Tradicionalmente, las conexiones entre el complemento y los servidores de control se cifraban con un certificado SSL, pero esto no impide que un propietario malintencionado de un servidor pueda interceptar y descifrar las comunicaciones. Por eso, TeleNVDA añade una capa de seguridad extra: el cifrado de datos. No lo hemos querido llamar cifrado de extremo a extremo, porque no lo es, pero impedirá que el propietario del servidor descifre lo que está pasando, así que en ese sentido se le parece. Cuando te conectes, comprobarás que, además del típico campo de clave, existe otro que permite introducir una contraseña adicional. Si lo rellenas, los datos se cifran con AES-GCM-256, de tal forma que sólo los miembros de la sesión que conozcan las dos contraseñas podrán unirse y participar con normalidad en el control remoto. Por desgracia, esta segunda contraseña acaba con la compatibilidad con el soporte remoto integrado en NVDA. Si necesitas garantizar compatibilidad, basta con no rellenarla. ¿Todavía no ves este campo? Es posible que tu TeleNVDA esté sin actualizar. Descarga aquí la versión más reciente Esto es todo por ahora. En breve volveremos para hablar de NVDA 2026.3.1 y sus correcciones de seguridad. ¡Hasta la próxima!

La entrada Nuevo curso de introducción a Python de NVDA.es y otras actualizaciones se publicó primero en NVDA en español .

es.title: Eva: la inteligencia artificial que adapta unas gafas inteligentes a las necesidades visuales de cada persona
es.summary: La inteligencia artificial continúa abriendo nuevas posibilidades para mejorar la autonomía de las personas con discapacidad visual. La última propuesta llega de la mano de Eyedaptic, una empresa especializada en tecnología de mejora visual que acaba de anunciar el lanzamiento de Eva, un asistente inteligente integrado en sus gafas EYE7. La principal novedad es que […] La entrada Eva: la inteligencia artificial que adapta unas gafas inteligentes a las necesidades visuales de cada persona se publicó primero en Conticgo .
es.body:
La inteligencia artificial continúa abriendo nuevas posibilidades para mejorar la autonomía de las personas con discapacidad visual. La última propuesta llega de la mano de Eyedaptic , una empresa especializada en tecnología de mejora visual que acaba de anunciar el lanzamiento de Eva, un asistente inteligente integrado en sus gafas EYE7.

La principal novedad es que Eva no se limita a describir lo que aparece delante de la cámara. También puede interpretar lo que necesita el usuario y actuar sobre las funciones de mejora visual de las gafas.

Hasta ahora, muchas herramientas de asistencia visual basadas en inteligencia artificial se han centrado en reconocer objetos, leer textos o describir escenas. Eva pretende ir un paso más allá.

Su funcionamiento se basa en la interpretación de instrucciones expresadas mediante lenguaje natural. Esto permite que la persona pueda comunicarse con las gafas de una manera más intuitiva, sin necesidad de aprender comandos específicos.

Por ejemplo, si alguien está intentando leer un cartel y dice «no consigo leer eso», Eva puede interpretar la petición y ajustar la experiencia visual para facilitar la lectura.

De esta manera, la tecnología no solo proporciona información sobre el entorno, sino que también puede modificar determinados ajustes de las gafas para adaptarlos a la actividad que se está realizando.

Según Eyedaptic, el asistente está diseñado para ayudar en diferentes situaciones de la vida cotidiana. Entre sus aplicaciones se encuentran:

Además, la compañía indica que Eva permite comunicarse en hasta 99 idiomas, lo que amplía sus posibilidades de utilización.

Eva está integrada en las gafas EYE7 de Eyedaptic, un dispositivo que combina tecnología de visión artificial, inteligencia artificial y realidad aumentada.

Estas gafas incorporan pantallas de alta definición y diferentes funciones de mejora visual. Su objetivo es ayudar a las personas con pérdida de visión central, especialmente aquellas con enfermedades de la retina como la degeneración macular asociada a la edad (DMAE).

Una de sus características es que las funciones pueden controlarse mediante instrucciones de voz, lo que permite interactuar con el dispositivo sin tener que manejar constantemente sus controles.

La llegada de Eva refuerza esta propuesta: la inteligencia artificial puede interpretar las necesidades de la persona y actuar directamente sobre las funciones de mejora visual disponibles.

Eyedaptic ha comunicado que, durante sus pruebas internas, Eva alcanzó una precisión superior al 99 % en lectura y del 97 % en la interpretación de comandos.

La empresa también señala que el asistente ya está disponible para los usuarios de EYE7 mediante una actualización remota del software, por lo que no es necesario adquirir unas gafas nuevas para incorporar esta función.

No obstante, estas cifras deben interpretarse con cautela. Se trata de resultados comunicados por el fabricante y no de una evaluación independiente publicada en una revista científica. Será necesario conocer su funcionamiento en situaciones reales y con diferentes perfiles de discapacidad visual para valorar su utilidad.

La propuesta de Eyedaptic refleja una tendencia cada vez más presente en la tiflotecnología: desarrollar herramientas que no solo proporcionen información sobre el entorno, sino que también se adapten a las necesidades de cada persona.

Para quienes tienen baja visión, poder ajustar una ayuda visual mediante una conversación sencilla puede facilitar determinadas actividades y reducir la necesidad de navegar por menús o aprender controles específicos.

Sin embargo, estas soluciones deben entenderse como herramientas de apoyo. No recuperan la visión ni sustituyen la rehabilitación visual, las ayudas ópticas o los dispositivos de movilidad.

El verdadero potencial de Eva dependerá de su rendimiento en el día a día, de su facilidad de uso y de cómo responda a las necesidades reales de las personas con discapacidad visual.

Si te ha gustado esta noticia no te pierdas las últimas novedades en tiflotectnología en nuestro apartado de noticias y redes sociales .

Fuente de la noticia: Eyedaptic .

en.title: Getting the Most Out of Vispero Companion: Tips and Best Practices
en.summary: Vispero Companion has grown from a helpful question-and-answer assistant into your one conversational home for all the AI features in JAWS. Whether you want to know how a feature works, get a description of a photo, explore a busy web page, or have a task done for you, it all happens in one familiar, accessible …
en.body:
Vispero Companion has grown from a helpful question-and-answer assistant into your one conversational home for all the AI features in JAWS. Whether you want to know how a feature works, get a description of a photo, explore a busy web page, or have a task done for you, it all happens in one familiar, accessible window. And because everything lives in a single conversation, you can keep asking follow-up questions without starting over. Here are some tips and best practices for getting the most out of Vispero Companion.

With Vispero Companion Actions, Companion does more than answer questions. Just ask, and it can help you:

You’re always in control. Companion only works when you ask, asks for your approval before executing important steps, and stops immediately when you press ESC.

The new Vispero Companion is available through the Early Adopter Program to users in the United States who are signed in to a Vispero account. To turn it on:

Once it’s on, press JAWS KEY+SPACEBAR followed by F1 to open Companion. The JAWS key is INSERT when using Desktop Keyboard layout, and CAPS LOCK when using Laptop layout.

Companion looks at what is on your screen to understand what you’re asking about. If the application window isn’t maximized, content can be cut off at the edges, and Companion may even pick up parts of other windows, such as the taskbar. Before you ask for help, place focus in the application you are working in and press WINDOWS+UP ARROW to maximize it.

When Companion carries out a task for you, it moves to your application and works there, much as you would. If you type, click, switch windows, or open another program while it’s working, you can change what Companion sees and pull it away from the task. It’s best to leave the keyboard and mouse alone until the task is complete, and Companion will let you know what it did once it’s finished. If you need to stop it, press ESC .

Once Companion takes its first action in an application, it stays in that app for the rest of the conversation. Outlook and Word, for example, are treated as separate applications. If you want help with something in a different program such as a web browser, close Companion and relaunch it from that application.

Companion opens in its own window, just like any other application on your computer. When you’re finished with it, press ALT+F4 to close it, the same way you would close any other window.

You don’t need to know which feature or setting does the job. Just tell Companion what you need, for example:

The more detail you give, the fewer attempts Companion needs to get it right. “For example, if you are asking Companion to help you book a flight, “Set the departure date to November 14” will work better than “Select November 14,” because Companion will know which type of date you want to set.

Companion keeps track of your current conversation while it is open so you can ask a follow-up question or for the next step without starting over. When you’re ready to change topics, select New Request for a fresh start or close and then relaunch Companion from a different application.

Already have the Picture Smart and Page Explorer commands in muscle memory? Keep using them. They now bring their results right into Companion, where you can ask follow-up questions.

Companion asks before doing anything that can’t easily be undone, such as submitting a form. Take a moment to read what it’s about to do before you confirm, and check its report when the task is finished so you know exactly where things stand.

Your feedback shapes what comes next for Companion. Select Give Feedback beside New Request to rate an answer or leave a comment. This button requires the Submit Anonymous Usage Data (telemetry) option to be turned on. If you’d prefer to leave it off, email your comments to SoftwareSuggestions@vispero.com . You can also select the Send Feedback button in the JAWS Early Adopter Program dialog.

For more information and a live demo, join us for our webinar on new features of JAWS, ZoomText, and Fusion 2027 at noon ET on Thursday, November 12. Have questions? Send an email to training@vispero.com .

es.title: GRETA & STARKS y ConUnPack impulsan la accesibilidad en las salas de cine españolas
es.summary: Las personas con discapacidad visual o auditiva podrán acceder a recursos de accesibilidad durante las sesiones habituales de cine gracias a soluciones como GRETA. La iniciativa se presenta en […] La entrada GRETA & STARKS y ConUnPack impulsan la accesibilidad en las salas de cine españolas se publicó primero en Conticgo .
es.body:
Las personas con discapacidad visual o auditiva podrán acceder a recursos de accesibilidad durante las sesiones habituales de cine gracias a soluciones como GRETA. La compañía tecnológica GRETA & STARKS y la distribuidora española ConUnPack han anunciado una alianza para impulsar el uso de esta tecnología en las salas españolas.

La iniciativa se presenta en MERCI 2026, el Mercado de Cine Independiente organizado por la Semana Internacional de Cine de Valladolid (SEMINCI) y la Asociación de Distribuidores Independientes Cinematográficos (ADICINE). El encuentro celebra su sexta edición del 28 al 30 de octubre en Valladolid.

GRETA es una aplicación móvil que permite utilizar diferentes recursos de accesibilidad sincronizados con la película. De este modo, cada espectador puede disfrutar de la sesión con los apoyos que necesita desde su propio dispositivo.

Entre sus principales funciones se encuentran:

Según explica la web oficial de GRETA , la aplicación utiliza el reconocimiento del sonido para sincronizar los recursos de accesibilidad con la película. Para utilizarla, basta con un teléfono móvil y, en el caso de la audiodescripción, unos auriculares.

Una de las principales ventajas de esta tecnología es que permite compartir una misma sesión cinematográfica sin necesidad de organizar proyecciones específicas para las personas con discapacidad visual o auditiva.

Cada espectador utiliza de forma individual el recurso que necesita. Así, una persona puede escuchar la audiodescripción mientras el resto del público sigue la película con el sonido habitual de la sala. Del mismo modo, los subtítulos adaptados pueden consultarse en la pantalla del teléfono móvil.

Esta posibilidad favorece una experiencia cinematográfica compartida y contribuye a reducir las barreras de acceso a la cultura.

No obstante, es importante tener en cuenta que la aplicación no garantiza la accesibilidad de todos los títulos. Para utilizar sus funciones, la película debe contar con los recursos correspondientes y estar disponible en el catálogo.

La alianza entre GRETA & STARKS y ConUnPack busca acercar estas soluciones a los profesionales de la exhibición cinematográfica en España.

Una de las ventajas del sistema es que no requiere instalar equipamiento específico en las salas para que cada usuario pueda utilizar la aplicación. Esto puede facilitar su incorporación en cines independientes y en espacios con menos recursos técnicos.

Sin embargo, la disponibilidad de películas accesibles y las condiciones de implantación del servicio siguen siendo factores importantes. Para ampliar su alcance, resulta fundamental que distribuidoras y exhibidores colaboren para ofrecer más títulos con audiodescripción y subtítulos adaptados.

La alianza se presenta en el marco de MERCI 2026, un encuentro profesional que reúne a representantes de la distribución, la exhibición y otros ámbitos de la industria audiovisual.

La programación oficial de SEMINCI incluye una presentación dedicada al cine accesible con la aplicación GRETA.

Este tipo de iniciativas pone de relieve la importancia de incorporar la accesibilidad a la distribución y exhibición cinematográfica. No basta con que una película llegue a las salas: también es necesario que las personas con diferentes necesidades sensoriales puedan acceder a su contenido.

Desde esta perspectiva, las herramientas de audio descripción y subtitulado adaptado representan un paso más hacia una cultura audiovisual inclusiva.

Si te ha gustado esta noticia no te pierdas las últimas novedades en tiflotectnología en nuestro apartado de noticias y redes sociales .

Fuentes: SEMINCI: programación profesional y MERCI 2026 , GRETA & STARKS: funcionamiento y características de la aplicación , Audiovisual451: información sobre la alianza entre ConUnPack y GRETA & STARKS , Ciné-Sens: información sobre el funcionamiento y la disponibilidad de recursos accesibles .

Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación , la rc 1 de NVDA 2026.3.1 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Se recomienda a todos los usuarios descargar esta versión y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, o por el sistema de informe de fallos de NV Access . A menos que se detecten fallos críticos de última hora, esta versión será idéntica a la versión final de NVDA 2026.3. Esta versión no es apta para entornos de producción. Al instalar esta rc te unirás al canal beta, y sólo recibirás avisos de actualización de compilaciones beta y candidatas a liberación (rc). El canal beta/rc siempre te mantendrá al día con la versión más reciente de NVDA. La última rc de un ciclo de liberación es idéntica a la última versión estable. Para regresar al canal de versiones estables, instala a mano la última versión estable.

Esta versión contiene un parche que resuelve incidencias de seguridad. También corrige un fallo introducido en NVDA 2026.3 con el conmutador de tareas de Windows 10. Se ha restaurado la voz de Espeak NG en portugués de Brasil al comportamiento que tenía en NVDA 2026.2. Para instalar esta rc, puedes configurar el canal «rc y beta» en el complemento Selector del canal de actualización y buscar actualizaciones desde el menú Ayuda de NVDA, o actualizar desde una beta anterior. Y como siempre, también puedes descargar manualmente el instalador de NVDA 2026.3.1 rc 1 . Su suma de comprobación SHA256, que te permitirá garantizar la integridad del archivo descargado, es 25761ace59812a5d60cc7282cca253c78d9293ce3e710eafb2b29783b5a1257c. ¡Feliz miércoles!

en.body:
JAWS, ZoomText, and Fusion 2027 are now available, offering new and exciting features that increase efficiency and productivity. Here’s a look at several highlights.

Vispero Companion now brings all your AI help together in one place. Whether you want to learn how a feature works, get a description of a photo, explore a busy web page, change a setting, or have a task performed for you, just ask Vispero Companion. Because everything lives in a single conversation, you can keep asking follow-up questions without starting over.

Note: The Vispero Companion website is still available for users who need to access product guidance from devices not running JAWS.

A Vispero Account is required to use the new features in the Vispero Companion update.

This feature is part of the Early Adopter Program, which provides access to new functionality that is still under active development. It is intended for users who want to try out upcoming features and provide feedback before they are fully released.

To enable this option:

In response to frequent requests from our community, JAWS now supports MuseScore, a popular free program for writing, editing, and playing back sheet music. Composers, music students, teachers, and hobbyists all use MuseScore to create everything from simple melodies to full orchestral scores, and JAWS users can now join them.

The Smoothing tab in the Preferences dialog box is now the Smoothing and Performance tab, with a new Performance group. The default, Best text quality, uses xFont and geometric smoothing to deliver the sharpest, clearest text ZoomText and Fusion offer, along with support for legacy reading. If ZoomText or Fusion feels slow on your system, you can choose Best performance, which uses geometric smoothing only for faster response, and then return to Best text quality at any time. You can also choose this option in the Startup Wizard.

ZoomText can now magnify apps that use screen-capture protection, so you can still read content that is already shown to you on screen. This is becoming increasingly important, as:

Photo Tracking identifies people, animals, food, and other objects in an image and moves the magnified view directly from one object to the next. You no longer need to zoom and pan across the whole picture to find what you want.

All recognition happens locally on your computer, so Photo Tracking works offline and is suitable for secure environments. It is available in ZoomText Magnifier/Reader, ZoomText Magnifier, and Fusion.

To learn more about all the new features and enhancements in this release, visit the What’s New pages for JAWS , ZoomText , and Fusion 2027.

Note: If you are running the latest version of JAWS, ZoomText, or Fusion and automatic updates are enabled, you can start the download and installation process from the notification.

In 2025, Apple introduced two brand new iPhone models: iPhone 16e, an entry-level model with most of the essential components of the more expensive iPhones of its generation; and iPhone Air, the thinnest-ever iPhone to date at the time. This year, Apple announced the iPhone Duo, the company's first-ever foldable iPhone and with it, a whole new form factor and way of using iPhone as we know it. In between the new iPhone models, Apple has, year-by-year, continued the steady evolution of its Pro and Pro Max phones. This year, for the first time, I had the opportunity to review both iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. One of the devices was a review unit on loan from Apple, whilst the other was the phone I purchased for myself. Being able to use both devices, one after the other, gave me a unique opportunity to evaluate them side-by-side, and I have a much deeper appreciation for each model and its strengths (and limitations). And after spending time with each phone, I came away with a surprising and yet inevitable conclusion: while iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max are similar, they are very different devices for very different use cases. Welcome Home: Apple Announces Updated HomePod Mini, Apple TV, All-New HomeView, and New Home Accessories By AppleVis | October 13, 2026 Apple today announced updated models of the HomePod Mini and Apple TV 4K ; as well as an all-new HomeView smart home hub and a collection of smart home accessories . iPhone 18 Pro: Thoughts and Experiences One Month After Upgrading from the iPhone 15 Pro By David Goodwin | October 18, 2026 I had never previously kept an iPhone for more than two years, but the iPhone 16 and 17 both came and went without me feeling any compelling need to upgrade from my iPhone 15 Pro. This year, with no regular iPhone 18 in the mix for consideration (for now, at least) and Apple's new folding iPhone Duo firmly outside my budget and interest, the choice was simpler than usual. It was the iPhone 18 Pro or nothing. With the iPhone 18 Pro priced at £1,199 here in the UK, "nothing" was a serious contender. So, I want to share how I reached my decision to upgrade, along with what I have learned from living with my new iPhone for the past month. TLDR: The iPhone 18 Pro is the best iPhone I've used, but it's not enough of a leap to justify upgrading from an iPhone 17 Pro, or possibly a 16 Pro. Welcome to the October 2026 edition of AppleVis Unlimited, your monthly digest of the latest and most notable content on the AppleVis website. This newsletter features a curated selection of community-submitted content, including new app entries, updates, news, podcast episodes, and popular discussions. We hope that you find this publication to be both helpful and informative. If you have any questions or feedback about this newsletter, please feel free to reach out using our Contact Form .

If you enjoy relaxing puzzle games that offer just the right amount of challenge, ReSort: Water Sort Puzzle App is definitely worth checking out. This delightful water-sorting game has you moving different colored water between tubes until each contains just one color. It starts out simple, but the puzzles get trickier as you progress, making it surprisingly addictive. With no timers or move limits, you can take your time and enjoy solving each puzzle at your own pace.

What really makes ReSort stand out for me is its wonderful sound design. I absolutely love the satisfying pouring sounds, gentle music, and little audio cues that make playing so enjoyable. Add in excellent VoiceOver support, daily challenges, unlockable sounds, and a developer who's been actively listening to the AppleVis community and making improvements based on their feedback, and there's plenty to appreciate.

Read more about ReSort here.

By Michael Hansen | October 8, 2026

[The last couple years have been big for iPhone.

In 2025, Apple introduced two brand new iPhone models: iPhone 16e, an entry-level model with most of the essential components of the more expensive iPhones of its generation; and iPhone Air, the thinnest-ever iPhone to date at the time. This year, Apple announced the iPhone Duo, the company's first-ever foldable iPhone and with it, a whole new form factor and way of using iPhone as we know it.

In between the new iPhone models, Apple has, year-by-year, continued the steady evolution of its Pro and Pro Max phones. This year, for the first time, I had the opportunity to review both iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. One of the devices was a review unit on loan from Apple, whilst the other was the phone I purchased for myself. Being able to use both devices, one after the other, gave me a unique opportunity to evaluate them side-by-side, and I have a much deeper appreciation for each model and its strengths (and limitations). And after spending time with each phone, I came away with a surprising and yet inevitable conclusion: while iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max are similar, they are very different devices for very different use cases. And only one of them is a device I would routinely recommend for most people.

I had never previously kept an iPhone for more than two years, but the iPhone 16 and 17 both came and went without me feeling any compelling need to upgrade from my iPhone 15 Pro. This year, with no regular iPhone 18 in the mix for consideration (for now, at least) and Apple's new folding iPhone Duo firmly outside my budget and interest, the choice was simpler than usual. It was the iPhone 18 Pro or nothing.

With the iPhone 18 Pro priced at £1,199 here in the UK, "nothing" was a serious contender. So, I want to share how I reached my decision to upgrade, along with what I have learned from living with my new iPhone for the past month.

TLDR: The iPhone 18 Pro is the best iPhone I've used, but it's not enough of a leap to justify upgrading from an iPhone 17 Pro, or possibly a 16 Pro.
