es.title: Las gafas inteligentes y la autonomía de las personas con discapacidad visual
es.summary: Las gafas inteligentes y la inteligencia artificial están abriendo nuevas posibilidades para las personas con discapacidad visual. Estas herramientas permiten reconocer establecimientos, leer textos y obtener descripciones del entorno mediante indicaciones de audio. El caso de Daniel Álvarez, que perdió la visión a los 15 años, muestra cómo la tecnología puede facilitar algunas tareas cotidianas. […] La entrada Las gafas inteligentes y la autonomía de las personas con discapacidad visual se publicó primero en Conticgo .
es.body:
Las gafas inteligentes y la inteligencia artificial están abriendo nuevas posibilidades para las personas con discapacidad visual. Estas herramientas permiten reconocer establecimientos, leer textos y obtener descripciones del entorno mediante indicaciones de audio.

El caso de Daniel Álvarez, que perdió la visión a los 15 años, muestra cómo la tecnología puede facilitar algunas tareas cotidianas. Su experiencia, recogida en un reportaje publicado por El Periódico el 25 de octubre de 2026, pone el foco en la utilidad de estos dispositivos para ganar autonomía.

Daniel Álvarez tiene 30 años, estudia Derecho en la Universitat Oberta de Catalunya (UOC) y trabaja en la ONCE. Tras perder la visión por un desprendimiento de retina irreversible, ha incorporado diferentes herramientas tecnológicas a su vida diaria.

Entre ellas destacan las gafas inteligentes, que incorporan cámaras y altavoces. Gracias a las aplicaciones compatibles, puede obtener información sobre los lugares y objetos que tiene delante.

Por ejemplo, estas gafas pueden ayudarle a distinguir si un establecimiento es un supermercado o una peluquería. También permiten leer textos, identificar colores y conocer detalles de objetos o prendas de ropa.

Sin embargo, sus posibilidades todavía tienen limitaciones. La descripción del entorno no siempre es completamente precisa y depende de la información que capta la cámara y de la interpretación que realiza el sistema.

Daniel utiliza, entre otras herramientas, ScribeMe, una aplicación que describe mediante inteligencia artificial las imágenes captadas por las cámaras de las gafas.

Las aplicaciones de inteligencia artificial no se limitan a describir objetos o espacios. También pueden contribuir a mejorar la accesibilidad de documentos y materiales educativos.

En el caso de Daniel, estas herramientas le permiten adaptar información que no está disponible en un formato accesible. Por ejemplo, puede transformar gráficos de ejercicios académicos en descripciones textuales que pueda comprender mediante su lector de pantalla.

Además, utiliza la inteligencia artificial para crear aplicaciones adaptadas a sus propias necesidades.

Estas posibilidades muestran que la tecnología puede facilitar el acceso a la educación, al trabajo y a la información. No obstante, para aprovecharlas es importante que las aplicaciones y los contenidos digitales sean accesibles desde su diseño.

Aunque las gafas inteligentes ofrecen nuevas posibilidades, no sustituyen a las herramientas tradicionales de orientación y movilidad.

Daniel continúa utilizando su bastón y las técnicas de orientación que conoce. Las gafas le aportan información adicional sobre su entorno, pero no garantizan una descripción completa ni una orientación espacial precisa.

Esta distinción es importante. Reconocer un establecimiento o leer un cartel puede resultar útil durante un desplazamiento, pero no equivale a detectar todos los obstáculos ni a identificar con precisión cada elemento de la vía pública.

Por ello, es fundamental conocer las capacidades y limitaciones de cada dispositivo antes de incorporarlo a las actividades cotidianas.

El Centro de Tiflotecnología e Innovación de la ONCE ha evaluado las gafas inteligentes Ray-Ban Meta y su aplicación Meta AI para analizar su posible utilidad para personas con ceguera o discapacidad visual grave. Su evaluación constituye una referencia especializada para conocer las posibilidades de esta tecnología.

La experiencia de Daniel refleja cómo la combinación de inteligencia artificial, dispositivos inteligentes y herramientas de accesibilidad puede facilitar distintas actividades de la vida diaria.

Sin embargo, la tecnología por sí sola no elimina todas las barreras. Es necesario que las soluciones sean fiables, accesibles y adaptadas a las necesidades reales de las personas con discapacidad visual.

También resulta importante que su desarrollo tenga en cuenta la experiencia de quienes las utilizan. La participación de las propias personas con discapacidad permite identificar necesidades concretas y mejorar la utilidad de estas herramientas.

En definitiva, las gafas inteligentes y la inteligencia artificial representan nuevas oportunidades para acceder a la información y desenvolverse con mayor autonomía. Su utilidad dependerá de que sigan mejorando y se integren como un complemento de los recursos de apoyo ya existentes.

Fuentes: El Periódico: reportaje sobre Daniel Álvarez y las nuevas tecnologías para personas con discapacidad , Centro de Tiflotecnología e Innovación de la ONCE: evaluación de las gafas inteligentes Ray-Ban Meta .

en.title: In-Process 2nd November 2026
en.summary: Happy All Saints Day / All Souls Day (I’m conscious of time zones, it is one of those two days for everyone, depending on where you are in the world). And wherever you are – Happy new NVDA release 🙂 Ok that was last week, but it’s like a birthday, the celebration doesn’t have to… Read More
en.body:
Happy All Saints Day / All Souls Day (I’m conscious of time zones, it is one of those two days for everyone, depending on where you are in the world). And wherever you are – Happy new NVDA release Ok that was last week, but it’s like a birthday, the celebration doesn’t have to end just because the calendar has ticked over This time around, we have:

The exciting news this time around is that NVDA 2026.3 is now available for download. This release includes significant performance improvements, improvements to NVDA’s dialogs, and expanded touch screen input.

Please note: We are aware of an issue for users of Brazilian Portuguese. We will have an update out shortly. Right now, affected users can use the NVDA 2026.3.1 Release Candidate or you can downgrade to NVDA 2026.2 .

Back to NVDA 2026.3: Several performance improvements have been made to reduce lag and improve responsiveness. NVDA now fetches and caches more information about controls in the background, improving performance in controls such as combo boxes and File Explorer. NVDA no longer causes File Explorer or other applications to crash when NVDA is exited or restarted. NVDA now recovers more quickly when an application stops responding, and will no longer freeze or flood the log with errors from unresponsive applications.

Context menus and keyboard shortcuts have been added to the Configuration Profiles, Input Gestures, and Speech Dictionaries dialogs, making these dialogs easier to use with the keyboard. It is also now possible to change an existing gesture directly in the Input Gestures dialog. The dialog used to present browsable messages has been modernized and now better supports resizing, maximizing, and minimizing.

Touch screen input has been significantly expanded. Sequential two-flick gestures now combine two flicks in quick succession into a single gesture, greatly increasing the number of bindable touch gestures. Edge gestures are also now supported, allowing gestures that start from any screen edge to be bound independently from the same gesture performed in the centre of the screen.

A new unassigned command has been added to move the mouse cursor to the centre of the magnified view. Windows OCR can now be used while the Screen Curtain or NVDA’s built-in Magnifier is active.

Liblouis has been updated with new Elfdalian, Sami, Maori, New Zealand Unified English Braille, Haitian Creole braille tables, a Norwegian table for Spanish text, and additional Swedish 6 and 8 dot variants. eSpeak NG has been updated with added support for Ligurian and Abkhaz.

Read the full details and download at: The NVDA 2026.3 Release Announcement .

Last fortnight we mentioned the new “Low Vision Users” page with information on various ways a low vision users might get the most out of NVDA. One big feature for this is, of course, the NVDA magnifier introduced in NVDA 2026.2. The post includes details of that, as well as including a link back to the previous blog post comparing the magnifier with the Windows magnifier , so you can judge which one will best meet your needs.

This week, I thought I’d pick out two other specific sections of that page for a closer look. Firstly, a short tip, but a useful one:

Copying information from web pages Traditionally, NVDA has only the text, not formatting or images, when copying information from web pages . It has also only worked when information was selected with the keyboard. NVDA has an option called “ Native Selection Mode ” which lets users copy formatting as well.

Importantly, if you select text with the mouse and then try to copy it with control+c , this will only work when using “Native Selection mode”. This mode can be toggled for individual pages with NVDA+shift+f10 . In NVDA 2026.3 and later, this mode can be enabled automatically in NVDA’s “Browse mode settings”.

This option in Browse mode settings is new for NVDA 2026.3 so well worth highlighting for anyone who can use it.

Visual Highlighter

NVDA’s Visual Highlight puts a border around the current object with focus, which can highlight what NVDA is reading. Press NVDA+control+g to open NVDA’s settings directly. Press control+tab to move between the different pages of settings. Use control+tab to move to the “Vision” page. The user guide describes the colours. Here are the descriptions: Solid blue highlights a combined navigator object and system focus location (e.g. because the navigator object follows the system focus) Dashed blue highlights just the system focus object Solid pink highlights just the navigator object Solid yellow highlights the virtual caret used in browse mode (where there is no physical caret such as in web browsers)

NVDA is able to move the focus around documents such as web pages where normally navigation doesn’t work. For instance, without NVDA running, you can’t arrow through a word on a web page. NVDA displays a pink line surrounding the current element with focus, such as a heading or paragraph of text. The yellow outline surrounds the character within that element which has focus (Usually the first character, unless you have moved the caret with, for instance, right arrow). A blue line surrounds the current interactive element (something you can press tab to move to). The “Basic Training for NVDA” module has more tips and techniques for navigating with the keyboard.

Screenshot of NVDA’s settings screen with a blue dotted highlight for the system focus around the “Enable Highlighting” option, and a pink highlight for the navigator object around the “Options:” heading. The mouse pointer is larger and coloured (refer to Other Windows Settings below).

We’ve made a couple of small changes to the navbar on the website this week. Hopefully all logical, but worth mentioning just in case: News: We removed the “Newsletter” and “Blog” items and replaced them with “News”. This is a menu which has options to “Subscribe” to news, check out our “Blog”, read “NVDA Stories” from users, or binge “All News Posts”. We’ve removed the “Create Account / Log In” option and in its place, the “Shop” item is a menu which lets you go to “Shop Training & Support”, “Create Account / Log In”, go to your “Cart” and “Download Purchases” (downloadable material you have previous purchased).

In addition, for those who need it, if you activate the header item for any of the navbar items with submenus (About, Get Help, News or Shop), it takes you to a page with links to each of the options for that section. What do you think? If you’ve got any feedback or any concerns, as always, please let us know.

Last fortnight we shared our new “ Accessibility Testing with NVDA ” package. There has been a lot of interest in this, but I did want to cover one question we did get: Does the Accessibility Testing with NVDA package lead into the “NVDA Expert Certification”?

The answer is “No”, as they are aimed at different groups of users:

NVDA Expert Certification is aimed at users who want to prove their screen reader skills (e.g. to potential employers) or professionals who teach or support NVDA users. The exam covers the skills an end user would need to know, but which are not important for accessibility testing. A good training module to lead into this exam is “ Basic Training for NVDA ”. This module teaches things such as how to navigate around text by word, sentence and paragraph, how to search for text on a page, and copy it. It also covers using tools such as OCR or object navigation for getting around places which aren’t as accessible.

“ Accessibility Testing with NVDA ” on the other hand, covers some NVDA skills, but places more emphasis on the information the screen reader is giving you which can help you ascertain the accessibility of your content. This module does not cover the finer points of searching or navigating by word, but notes the way nonvisual users can locate important information on a page, and the kinds of elements which can be useful for this. Instead of covering features for accessing inaccessible content, Accessibility Testing with NVDA highlights ways of checking that your content is accessible, and what to do if it is not.

If you are an accessibility professional who wants a way to show the world that accessibility is important to you and that you do incorporate NVDA in your testing, then we do have good news. The “ Accessibility Testing with NVDA ” package includes a badge you can add to your email signature, your website or elsewhere. We encourage you to display it proudly!

That’s all for this week. We’ll be back in a fortnight with more. Do try out NVDA 2026.3 if you haven’t already. We hope you enjoy the performance and other improvements, and we look forward to sharing more highlights with you soon.

en.body:
ZoomText and Fusion are powerful accessibility tools designed for people with low vision. ZoomText is a screen magnifier and reader, while Fusion combines all of ZoomText’s features with the full JAWS screen reader, offering both magnification and speech.

In honor of National Disability Employment Awareness Month, our Workplace Ready blog series has run throughout October, with a new post every Thursday spotlighting ZoomText and Fusion features that help you be more productive at work. This is the final post in the series. Last week, we shared practical tips for tackling online tasks. This week, we’ll show you how to set up ZoomText and Fusion to work the way you do.

The features we’ve covered this month are most helpful when they’re tuned to the way you work. Taking a few minutes to customize ZoomText and Fusion is one of the most important steps you can take for workplace productivity. The right magnification level, colors, and view for each task mean less time adjusting settings and more time getting things done.

Personalized settings remove the small points of friction that add up over a busy day. When your tools are ready the moment you open an application, you can move between tasks smoothly and work more efficiently and independently. This week, we’ll look at how to save settings for each application, set up your preferred colors and display options, and use touch screen support on compatible devices.

The settings that work well in one program may not be the best choice for another. With Application Settings, you can save unique magnification and enhancement settings for each application you use. Once saved, ZoomText and Fusion automatically load the right settings as you switch between programs, so you don’t have to stop and adjust your view every time you change tasks.

To create Application Settings, open the application and adjust magnification, cursor, or mouse settings to meet your needs, then open the ZoomText menu, choose Application Settings , and save the current settings for that application. To keep your general preferences for every other program, choose Configurations > Save As Default from the ZoomText menu.

Here’s how this might look across a typical workday:

When you move from writing a report in Word to answering email in Outlook, ZoomText and Fusion switch to your Outlook settings automatically. When you come back, your Word settings are right where you left them.

The right colors can make text easier to read and reduce eye strain over a long workday. Color Enhancements let you choose from a variety of preset color schemes, such as inverted brightness or high-contrast combinations, or create your own custom colors. To pick a scheme, select the arrow next to the Color button on the Magnifier toolbar tab. Press CAPS LOCK+C to toggle color enhancements on and off. When you find a combination you like, save it as part of your default configuration or your Application Settings so it’s ready when you need it.

Different tasks also call for different views. ZoomText and Fusion offer several zoom window types for a single monitor: Full , Overlay , Lens , Line , and Docked (Top, Bottom, Left, or Right). Full magnifies the entire screen, which works well for reading documents. Docked keeps part of the screen at normal size, which can be helpful when you want to see the whole layout of an application while magnifying the area you’re working in. Press CAPS LOCK+Z to cycle through the zoom window types, or select the Window button on the Magnifier toolbar tab to choose one.

If you use more than one monitor, ZoomText and Fusion can extend your workspace across two displays. When your monitors are set to extend your desktop, you can choose from these zoom window types:

In the MultiView modes, press CAPS LOCK+V to switch the active view. For more options, such as keeping both views at the same magnification level, select Window > Settings on the Magnifier toolbar tab and choose Multiple Monitor Options .

If you work on a touch screen laptop or tablet, you can control ZoomText and Fusion with gestures. Touch Screen Support works on Windows devices that support at least five simultaneous touch points.

To get started, open the ZoomText menu and choose Preferences > Touch Screen Support > Enable Touch Icon . The Touch Icon lets you switch between two modes:

Double-tap the Touch Icon with one finger to switch modes. To switch for just a moment, hold one finger on the icon, then lift it to return to the previous mode.

In ZoomText Touch Mode, try these gestures:

A few tips can make touch more comfortable at work. Choose a Touch Icon size and color that are easy for you to see from Preferences > Touch Screen Support on the ZoomText menu. Move the icon out of the way by holding one finger on it and dragging it along the edge of the screen. If you share time between a keyboard and touch, keep the icon in Windows Touch Mode when you’re tapping through applications and switch to ZoomText Touch Mode when you want to zoom or pan.

That brings our Workplace Ready series to a close. Throughout October, we’ve explored how ZoomText and Fusion can help you work more productively and independently. Here’s a look back at what we covered:

There’s always more to discover. Take some time to explore additional features and try new settings as your work changes. For tutorials, webinars, and other learning materials, visit our training page. Thank you for following along this month, and keep thriving in your workplace!

Have questions? Email training@vispero.com .

es.title: Duke investiga una IA en el móvil para mejorar la asistencia visual
es.summary: La inteligencia artificial para personas con discapacidad visual sigue avanzando. Un equipo de investigación vinculado a Duke University, en Estados Unidos, trabaja en un sistema capaz de detectar obstáculos, identificar objetos que se aproximan y describir el entorno mediante indicaciones de audio. El proyecto combina unas gafas con cámara y un teléfono móvil. Su objetivo […] La entrada Duke investiga una IA en el móvil para mejorar la asistencia visual se publicó primero en Conticgo .
es.body:
La inteligencia artificial para personas con discapacidad visual sigue avanzando. Un equipo de investigación vinculado a Duke University, en Estados Unidos, trabaja en un sistema capaz de detectar obstáculos, identificar objetos que se aproximan y describir el entorno mediante indicaciones de audio.

El proyecto combina unas gafas con cámara y un teléfono móvil. Su objetivo es facilitar información útil durante los desplazamientos y otras actividades cotidianas.

Además, los investigadores quieren ejecutar el modelo de inteligencia artificial directamente en el teléfono, de esta forma, el sistema podría funcionar sin depender de servidores externos para procesar las imágenes.

La propuesta utiliza gafas inteligentes equipadas con una cámara que captura el entorno de la persona usuaria. Las imágenes se envían al sistema de inteligencia artificial para analizar lo que ocurre alrededor.

A partir de esa información, el sistema busca proporcionar indicaciones de audio sobre posibles peligros y elementos relevantes del entorno.

Entre las funciones que investiga el equipo se encuentran:

Estas funciones pretenden complementar las herramientas de movilidad existentes, como el bastón blanco o el perro guía. No buscan sustituirlas.

Una de las principales líneas de trabajo es conseguir que el sistema procese las imágenes en el propio teléfono, en lugar de enviarlas continuamente a servidores externos.

Para ello, el equipo ha trabajado con un modelo de inteligencia artificial comprimido, denominado modelo de 0,5 mil millones de parámetros. Esta reducción busca que el sistema pueda ejecutarse en un dispositivo móvil con recursos limitados.

Los investigadores han comparado un sistema básico de alertas basado en reglas con este nuevo modelo, diseñado para interpretar mejor el contexto de los posibles peligros.

Sin embargo, el equipo todavía debe completar un paso fundamental: exportar el modelo para que funcione directamente en el dispositivo. Por tanto, la asistencia inteligente sin conexión a internet es un objetivo del proyecto, no una función que deba darse por plenamente disponible.

Ejecutar la inteligencia artificial en el móvil puede ofrecer varias ventajas para las tecnologías de apoyo a la discapacidad visual.

En primer lugar, el sistema podría responder con mayor rapidez al no tener que enviar cada imagen a un servidor remoto y esperar su respuesta. En una situación de desplazamiento, reducir ese tiempo puede ser especialmente importante.

Además, el procesamiento local permitiría reducir la dependencia de una conexión a internet. Esto facilitaría el uso de determinadas funciones en lugares con poca cobertura.

Por último, mantener las imágenes en el propio dispositivo podría mejorar la privacidad, ya que reduciría la necesidad de transmitir vídeos del entorno a servidores externos. No obstante, la protección de los datos también dependerá del funcionamiento completo de la aplicación y de cómo gestione la información.

Estas ventajas son posibilidades técnicas que deberán comprobarse mediante pruebas del sistema terminado.

Aunque la investigación abre nuevas posibilidades, todavía es necesario evaluar el funcionamiento del sistema en condiciones reales.

Por ejemplo, detectar un obstáculo en una imagen no garantiza que se identifique correctamente durante un desplazamiento. Los cambios de iluminación, los espacios concurridos y los objetos difíciles de distinguir pueden afectar a los resultados.

También será importante comprobar la rapidez de las alertas, la autonomía de la batería y la facilidad de uso de las gafas. Además, los avisos deberán ser claros y oportunos para no sobrecargar de información sonora a la persona usuaria.

Por ello, las pruebas con personas ciegas y con baja visión serán fundamentales para determinar si esta tecnología aporta beneficios reales en la vida cotidiana.

La investigación de Duke University refleja una tendencia creciente en tiflotecnología: desarrollar sistemas de inteligencia artificial más pequeños y capaces de funcionar en dispositivos portátiles.

Si se consigue ejecutar el modelo directamente en el móvil, la propuesta podría reducir la dependencia de internet y facilitar respuestas más inmediatas sobre el entorno.

Aun así, el proyecto sigue en desarrollo y todavía debe demostrar su eficacia en situaciones reales. Su evolución permitirá conocer hasta qué punto la inteligencia artificial local puede complementar las ayudas de movilidad y contribuir a la autonomía de las personas con discapacidad visual.

Fuentes: Duke University, Rhodes Information Initiative — Data+: AI-Powered Hazard Detection for the Visually Impaired (22 de julio de 2026)

en.title: Apple Introduces Updated iMac and MacBook Pros with Performance and Connectivity Improvements, a Touchscreen for the High-End MacBook Pro, and More
en.summary: On the heels of introducing the 8th generation iPad Mini , Apple this week updated the iMac and MacBook Pro, bringing faster chips, improved connectivity, and, for the first time, a touchscreen to the MacBook Pro. iMac Featuring up to a 12-core CPU, the new iMac with M6, according to Apple's press release , delivers: Up to 2.5x faster performance in apps like Microsoft Excel, compared to iMac with M1, and up to 1.5x faster performance than M4. Up to 3.3x faster graphics performance for tasks including photo editing in Affinity, compared to iMac with M1, and up to 2x faster performance than M4. Up to 12x faster on-device AI performance for prompt processing in LM Studio, compared to iMac with M1, and up to 5x faster performance than M4. Up to 2x higher gaming performance with ray tracing compared to M4. Up to 2x faster SSD read and write performance. With the N1 wireless networking chip, the new iMac supports Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, and up to a 2.5 gigabit Ethernet port, included with the power adapter. The iMac with M6 is made with 100 percent recycled aluminum in the stand, 100 percent recycled rare earth elements in all magnets, 100 percent recycled gold plating and tin solder in all Apple-designed circuit boards, and is manufactured with 40 percent renewable electricity. It can be pre-ordered from Apple in green, yellow, orange, pink, purple, blue, and silver starting today for a starting price of US $1499, and will begin shipping to customers on Friday, November 6. MacBook Pro In addition to the iMac, Apple updated the base 14-inch MacBook Pro with the M6 chip, N1 wireless networking chip, and up to 170 GBPS of unified memory bandwidth. The MacBook Pro with M6, according to Apple's press release delivers: Up to 13x faster time to first token performance for LLM prompt processing compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.3x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5. Up to 11.7x faster render performance with ray tracing in Blender compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.3x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5. Up to 3.3x faster image-processing performance in Affinity compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.2x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5. Up to 2.5x faster project build performance when compiling code in Xcode compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.3x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5. Apple also claims the 12-core GPU paired with the dual 16-core neural engine features up to 30 percent faster graphics performance compared to M5, as well as up to 25 percent faster performance for on-device AI workloads. The new MacBook Pro also features the N1 wireless networking chip, bringing Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 support. The MacBook Pro with M6 is made with 45 percent recycled content overall, including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure, 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery, and 100 percent recycled tantalum in multiple capacitors, and is manufactured with 60 percent renewable electricity across the supply chain. It can be pre-ordered from Apple starting today for a starting price of US $1999, and will begin shipping to customers on Friday, November 6. Apple has also introduced new high-end 14 and 16-inch MacBook Pros , bringing a thinner and lighter design, a redesigned thermal architecture, a new speaker design, hinge improvements, and, for the first time on a Mac, an OLED touchscreen and Dynamic Island. With the Dynamic Island, users will be able to view Live Activities, answer calls, and use Siri and Spotlight. At the time of publication, we do not know how VoiceOver or any other macOS accessibility tool will work with touch controls. The MacBook Pro with PROOLEDXDR display continues to use the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, but it now features a redesigned thermal architecture that Apple claims better redirects air away from the display, helping to prevent it from getting warm to the touch while maintaining sustained performance. The MacBook Pro with PROOLEDXDR display is made with 55 percent recycled content overall, including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure, 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery, and recycled tantalum in multiple capacitors, and is manufactured with 45 percent renewable electricity across the supply chain. It can be pre-ordered from Apple starting today for a starting price of US $2899, and will begin shipping to customers on Friday, November 6.

en.title: Announcing AnonyMouse's App Pick of the Month for October 2026: ReSort: Water Sort Puzzle App
en.summary: Welcome to the October 2026 installment of AnonyMouse's App Pick of the Month, where each month I highlight a new or noteworthy app. This month's pick is ReSort: Water Sort Puzzle App, a fun and relaxing water-sorting puzzle game that has quickly become one of my favorites. I know, I know. Another game for my App Pick of the Month! I realize not everyone here is a gamer, and I'm sorry for picking yet another one. But we've had so many fun new games coming our way lately, I just can't help myself! ReSort was simply too much fun to pass up. Maybe next month I'll pick something different. No promises, though! About ReSort ReSort is a puzzle game where you sort different-colored water into separate tubes until each tube contains just one color. Sounds simple enough, right? Well, it starts out that way, but things get trickier as you progress. Before long, you're moving water back and forth, trying to figure out your next move without getting yourself stuck. What I really enjoy is that there's no rush with ReSort. No timers, no move limits, and no pressure. You can take your time and figure things out at your own pace. But don't mistake relaxing for easy! Some puzzles can really get you scratching your head, and finally solving one that's been giving you trouble is incredibly satisfying. There's plenty to keep you busy, too. Along with the regular levels, ReSort offers daily puzzles with different difficulty settings and a larger Sunday challenge. You can also earn stars, work your way through different ranks, and unlock additional sounds as you progress. Accessibility is another reason ReSort stands out. The game was designed with VoiceOver in mind, with announcements for the colors and their positions in each tube. And I have to say, I absolutely love the sounds in this game! From the satisfying sound of pouring water to the little audio cues and gentle music, everything adds to the experience. It's one of those games where the sounds make playing that much more enjoyable. I also love that you can customize them to your liking. Something else I really appreciate is the developer's involvement with the AppleVis community. Since introducing ReSort in the AppleVis forum , the developer has been actively listening to feedback and making improvements. Suggestions from community members have already led to different daily puzzle difficulties, iCloud syncing, more sound options, and adjustable tube sizes for low-vision players. I love seeing developers take our community's suggestions seriously, especially when those suggestions turn into actual features so quickly. It's wonderful to see that kind of engagement. Why I'm Picking ReSort This Month For me, ReSort is just plain fun. It's easy to learn, challenging enough to keep me interested, and relaxing enough to enjoy whenever I have a few minutes to spare. And that's where the trouble starts! I'll tell myself I'm only going to play a couple of levels, and before I know it, I've played several more. There's always another puzzle waiting, and I can't seem to resist finding out whether I can solve it. I also appreciate getting to enjoy this type of game with VoiceOver. Water-sorting games have been around for years, but finding one that's this accessible isn't something I take for granted. Between the enjoyable gameplay, wonderful sounds, thoughtful accessibility, and a developer who's genuinely listening to our community, ReSort has earned its place as my October App Pick of the Month. If you enjoy puzzle games, or just want something relaxing that gives your brain a little workout, I definitely recommend giving ReSort a try. Just don't blame me if you find yourself playing longer than you planned! Download the App ReSort: Water Sort Puzzle App is available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad. The first 10 levels are free, with a one-time purchase to unlock the remaining levels. There are no ads or subscriptions, and all accessibility features are included for free. Now It's Your Turn Have you tried ReSort yet? Are you finding it as addictive as I am? How far have you made it in the game? I'd love to hear what you think and what other apps or games you've been enjoying this month. Let me know in the comments. I always enjoy hearing what everyone else is playing and discovering!

en.title: Apple Introduces Updated iPad Mini with Thinner and Lighter Design, Upgraded Display and Camera, A20 Pro chip, N1 and C2 Networking Chips, and More
en.summary: Apple today introduced the new 8th-generation iPad mini, bringing a thinner and lighter design, an 8.5-inch OLED display, A20 Pro chip, N1 and C2 networking chips, a new audio system, and more. With the new design, iPad mini features an upgraded 8.5-inch OLED display while maintaining its existing footprint, thanks to 24 percent thinner bezels. A new audio system that integrates components between the display and enclosure removes the speaker holes and contributes to an IP67 water and dust resistance rating, a first for any iPad. With A20 Pro, Apple claims iPad mini delivers up to 4.5X faster AI performance, up to 2.7X faster graphics performance, and up to 60 percent faster performance for everyday tasks compared to the previous generation. In addition, the N1 wireless networking chip adds Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread support to iPad mini, and cellular models of the device include Apple's C2 modem, which Apple claims delivers up to 50 percent faster data speeds compared to the previous generation. The 12MP Center Stage front camera has been moved to the landscape edge of the device, as it is on other iPad models. Apple touts this as beneficial for FaceTime calls and collaboration. Apple additionally claims that the new Adaptive True Tone flash improves photos and document scanning. To compliment the new iPad mini, Apple has also introduced a new Smart Folio magnetic cover that features "TechWoven" fabric. The new iPad mini is made with 35 percent recycled content overall, including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure and 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery, and is manufactured with 40 percent renewable energy across the supply chain. It can be pre-ordered from Apple starting Wednesday, October 28 in midnight and starlight finishes for a starting price of US $699, and will begin shipping to customers on Friday, November 6.

en.title: Apple Releases iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2 with Expanded Language Support for Siri AI, Profiles for the TV App, Bug Fixes, and More
en.summary: Apple has today released iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2 to the public, bringing Siri AI support for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish, support for multiple profiles in the TV app, anniversary alerts in Call Context, and various bug fixes. Apple has also released iOS 26.7.2 for devices not running iOS 27. Resolved Accessibility Bugs Our experience is that the following accessibility bugs have been resolved or meaningfully improved in iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2: The changes made to VoiceOver's audio profile in iOS 27.0 and iPadOS 27.0 appear to have been reverted. Using the Dot Pad, The f1 and f4 keys now pan the larger 20x8 display correctly. Also using the Dot Pad, the triangular-shaped buttons now pan the 20-cell display as expected. The gesture, keyboard shortcut, and Perkins-style keyboard commands for Touch and Sound Curtain once again work as expected. Navigating and selecting text with a hardware keyboard is significantly improved. VoiceOver recognizing and speaking when an item state changes or when information has updated is significantly improved, however, the issue may still occur occasionally. The buttons to switch between All and Missed in the Phone app's Classic view, as well as the ones to switch between Start Page, Bookmarks, Reading List, and History in Safari, now work. The "Clear All" rotor action in Notification Center once again works. The "Direct Touch" option in VoiceOver's Quick Settings panel once again works. It is once again possible to swipe from the battery indicator to other items on the status bar when an app is opened. VoiceOver's "copy to clipboard" function now only copies the desired content rather than the full semantic markup. The Call button on the keypad in the Phone app is once again labeled correctly. The "Delete" action in the rotor for conversations in the Siri app is no longer doubled. It is no longer necessary to remove the previously-assigned command in VoiceOver Settings before a new one will work. VoiceOver once again speaks the time at the top of the hour correctly when in 24 hour mode. The "Show Bookmarks" button is once again labeled correctly when the Safari toolbar is set to "Bottom." VoiceOver now works in the "Device Diagnostics" option in the Recovery Menu. The VoiceOver per-voice equalizer now works as expected. VoiceOver once again behaves as expected when editing text and placing focus on a combo box. The Camera App no longer contains extraneous UI elements for editing camera controls when Edit Mode is not active. When swiping through the Lock Screen, VoiceOver focus once again behaves in a consistent and predictable way. We are additionally aware of two new bugs in this release: When navigating an expanded conversation in the messages table in Mail with the up and down arrow keys, VoiceOver speaks “label.text.blank” before each message. When Tabbing past the subject field in Mail’s “New Message” window, focus jumps to the “Format” radio button in the toolbar instead of the next focusable element in the window, requiring you to press the Tab key several additional times to get to the message body text field. Write with Siri is available right from the new formatting bar when you compose a message in Mail. FaceTime FaceTime links make it easier to join calls directly from your Apple TV. Sign language interpreter and captioning support lets you add third-party services to your calls. Screen Savers Photo personalization lets you use your iPhone to choose specific photos for your screen saver without sharing your full library with Apple TV. Shuffle option lets you enjoy different screen saver categories as your Apple TV cycles through them. Find My Find My support lets you locate your Siri Remote (2nd generation) or later using your iPhone. HomePod Software 27.2 HomePod software version 27.2 brings the new Sound Glow visual experience, home theater surround sound with Apple TV 4K (4th generation), and support for using HomePod speakers with your Mac, along with bug fixes and security updates for your HomePod. Sound Glow on HomePod mini, HomePod mini 2, and HomePod (2nd generation) turns the top of HomePod into a visual display that pulses and glows in sync with your media and shows matching light animations for soundscapes. Home theater surround sound supports connecting four HomePod speakers to Apple TV 4K (4th generation) for an immersive listening experience. Requires matching front and rear pairs of HomePod mini 2 or HomePod (2nd generation). HomePod speakers with your Mac lets you set HomePod as the audio output for everything you do on your Mac, with a responsive and persistent AirPlay connection. Lock controls let you disable the touch controls on top of HomePod to prevent accidental taps from pausing music, skipping songs, or changing the volume. To install the update, your Watch must be connected to its charger and have at least 50% battery power. To install tvOS 27.2, on Apple TV 4K or Apple TV HD, go to the Settings channel, then look for the System section near the bottom. From here, look for Software Updates under Maintenance, then select Update Software and Download and Install. Wait for your Apple TV to download the update. Don't disconnect or unplug your Apple TV until the update completes. By default, HomePod and HomePod mini automatically install new software updates, but you can manually check for updates in the Home app on your iPhone, iPad, or Mac.

es.body:
Tras 6 versiones beta y una candidata a liberación, NV Access ha anunciado mediante esta publicación que ya se encuentra disponible para su descarga la versión final de NVDA 2026.3, el lector de pantalla gratuito y de código abierto para Microsoft Windows. Se recomienda a todos los usuarios actualizar a esta nueva versión, cuyo uso se considera apto también en entornos de producción.

Esta versión incluye importantes mejoras de rendimiento, mejoras en los cuadros de diálogo de NVDA y una mayor compatibilidad con la entrada mediante pantalla táctil. Se han introducido varias mejoras de rendimiento para reducir el retraso y mejorar la capacidad de respuesta. NVDA ahora recopila y almacena en caché más información sobre los controles en segundo plano, lo que mejora el rendimiento en controles como los cuadros combinados y el Explorador de archivos. NVDA ya no provoca que el Explorador de archivos u otras aplicaciones se cuelguen al salir de NVDA o al reiniciarlo. Ahora, NVDA se recupera más rápidamente cuando una aplicación deja de responder y ya no se bloquea ni satura el registro con errores de las aplicaciones que no responden. Se han añadido menús de contexto y atajos de teclado a los cuadros de diálogo «Perfiles de configuración», «Gestos de entrada» y «Diccionarios del habla», lo que facilita el uso de estos cuadros de diálogo con el teclado. Ahora también es posible modificar un gesto ya existente directamente en el cuadro de diálogo «Gestos de entrada». Se ha actualizado el cuadro de diálogo que se utiliza para mostrar los mensajes que se pueden consultar y ahora permite cambiar el tamaño, maximizar y minimizar con mayor facilidad. Se han ampliado considerablemente las opciones de introducción de datos mediante pantalla táctil. Los gestos secuenciales de dos flicks combinan ahora dos flicks consecutivos en un único gesto, lo que aumenta considerablemente el número de gestos táctiles a los que se pueden asignar acciones. Ahora también se admiten los gestos desde los bordes, lo que permite asociar gestos que se inician desde cualquier borde de la pantalla de forma independiente de los mismos gestos realizados en el centro de la pantalla. Se ha añadido una nueva orden sin asignar para desplazar el cursor del ratón al centro de la vista ampliada. Ahora es posible utilizar el OCR de Windows mientras están activos la Cortina de pantalla o el magnificador integrado de NVDA. Se ha actualizado Liblouis con nuevas tablas de braille en elfdaliano, sami, maorí, braille unificado neozelandés, criollo haitiano, una tabla noruega para texto en español y variantes adicionales suecas de 6 y 8 puntos. Se ha actualizado eSpeak NG para que sea compatible con el ligur y el abjasio. Consulta todas las novedades aquí Tan pronto como actualices NVDA, no olvides reiniciar el equipo. El reinicio garantiza que se pueden actualizar archivos que antes no se podían modificar porque estaban abiertos para escritura. En la práctica, al reiniciar vuelven a funcionar aplicaciones basadas en Electron, tales como Teams, Dropbox o Google Drive, y dejan de producirse comportamientos extraños con el explorador de archivos, Thunderbird, Office y algunos navegadores. Reiniciar es lo primero que debes hacer antes de informar de cualquier fallo. Hazlo pulsando windows+d para ir al escritorio, alt+f4, e intro sobre la opción Reiniciar. Puedes descargar NVDA 2026.3, así como las últimas versiones compatibles con sistemas antiguos y material útil para desarrolladores, desde nuestra página de descargas . La suma SHA256 de NVDA 2026.3, que se usa para garantizar la integridad de la descarga, es a8a87cb823da0c62cfbae4a444ae5ae238d54dc82ad6d46d3fdb3fef082799b2. Si tienes una versión estable anterior, también puedes actualizar automáticamente desde el menú Ayuda. Y desde la rc1, con el complemento Selector del canal de actualización, se puede hacer del mismo modo configurando previamente el canal estable. Si todavía no conoces NVDA y quieres leer algo más sobre él antes de probarlo, te recomendamos consultar la guía de usuario y la referencia rápida de órdenes . Si te gustan nuestros proyectos y el contenido que ofrecemos, plantéate contribuir mensualmente con una pequeña cantidad. Tan sólo un euro es capaz de marcar la diferencia y ayudarnos a mejorar. Visita la página de donaciones para obtener más información, o la tienda para hacerte con libros de formación traducidos y sintetizadores de voz de alta calidad. ¡Feliz lunes!

en.title: Access More Online with ZoomText and Fusion
en.summary: ZoomText and Fusion are powerful accessibility tools designed for people with low vision. en.body:
ZoomText and Fusion are powerful accessibility tools designed for people with low vision. ZoomText is a screen magnifier and reader, while Fusion combines all of ZoomText’s features with the full JAWS screen reader, offering both magnification and speech.

Since October is National Disability Employment Awareness Month, we want to take this opportunity to spotlight powerful features of ZoomText and Fusion that will help you be more productive in the workplace. This blog series will run throughout October, with a new post every Thursday featuring helpful information and practical tips to make the most of ZoomText and Fusion as you work. Last week, we followed a typical workday from Word to Teams. This week, we’ll provide practical tips for using ZoomText and Fusion when tackling online tasks.

So much of today’s work happens in a web browser: company intranets, online forms, dashboards, and web-based apps for everything from timesheets to project tracking. Whether you’re researching a topic, filling out a form, or checking the latest numbers, having ZoomText or Fusion set up to support the way you browse can make all the difference. This week, we’ll look at how these tools can help you move around websites, find information quickly, read web content comfortably, and keep an eye on the details you check most often.

Busy web pages are easier to work with when you can see exactly where you are. With ZoomText and Fusion, you can quickly adjust your magnification level or switch between different zoom window types, like Lens or Line view, to focus on the part of the page that matters most. Lens and Line are available when you use a single monitor. Lens works like a magnifying glass. It displays a magnified rectangle that follows the mouse pointer. Line works like a magnifying ruler. It displays a magnified horizontal strip that moves up and down the screen and enlarges whatever is directly beneath it.

Press CAPS LOCK+Z to cycle through the available zoom window types until you reach the one you want.

Focus enhancements highlight the item you are on as you navigate using the Tab and arrow keys through links, buttons, and form fields, making it easy to keep your place even at high magnification. Press CAPS LOCK+F to toggle focus enhancements on and off. You can also customize the appearance of the focus locator to suit your needs.

Fusion users can take advantage of the JAWS Virtual Cursor, which simulates a system cursor and lets you read and move through a web page the same way you would a document. The Virtual Cursor is on by default when you are on a web page.

Quick Navigation keys let you jump straight to the content you need without scanning the entire page. Press H to move to the next heading, F to move to the next form field, and L to move to the next list. Add SHIFT to any of these keys, such as SHIFT+H , to move backward. Press TAB to move through links and form controls.

Long pages and crowded web apps can hide the information you are trying to locate. The ZoomText Finder tool lets you search for words or phrases on web pages and in documents. Open Finder from the ZoomText toolbar, type your search term, and use the navigation buttons to jump between results. ZoomText brings each match into the magnified view, so you don’t have to pan around the page looking for it.

Fusion users can use the Find command to locate specific text on a web page. Press CTRL+F to open the Find dialog, type your search term, and press ENTER to jump to the next occurrence. Press F3 to navigate to the next occurrence of that text.

For even faster navigation, JAWS can list every link or heading on a page. Press CAPS LOCK+F7 to open the Links List or CAPS LOCK+F6 to open the Headings List, then choose an item and press ENTER to jump directly to the section or link you need.

Articles, reports, and long web pages are easier to get through when you don’t have to read every word on screen. AppReader reads documents, web pages, and email aloud while you follow along or rest your eyes. It can read from beginning to end, skim forward and backward, or read just the text you select with the mouse. AppReader reads text aloud in three modes: App View reads directly in the source application without changing your view, Text View reformats the text with your choice of fonts, colors, and magnification for easier reading, and the SpeakIt Tool reads any text on the screen that you select by clicking and dragging. Press CAPS LOCK+ALT+A to launch App View. Press CAPS LOCK+ALT+T to launch Text View. Press CAPS LOCK+ALT+S to launch the SpeakIt Tool.

To start reading at a specific word on a web page, point to it with the mouse and press CAPS LOCK+ALT+LEFT-CLICK . Text View is especially helpful on cluttered pages, since it strips away the layout and shows just the text in a format that’s comfortable for you.

Background Reader in ZoomText lets you listen to web content while you keep working on other tasks. Select and copy the text you want to hear, then press CAPS LOCK+CTRL+B to start Background Reader. You can continue working in other applications while the content is read aloud.

Fusion users can use the JAWS Say All command to read an entire article from the cursor position. Press CAPS LOCK+DOWN ARROW to start continuous reading, and press CTRL to stop. This is perfect for reviewing long articles or reports.

Many of us return to the same web pages and apps every day to check a status, a total, or a notification. Reading Zones put that information one keystroke away. A reading zone is a defined area of an application window that ZoomText can display, speak, or both, at the press of a hotkey. You can set up as many as 10 zones.

To create a reading zone, open the web page or application, press CAPS LOCK+ALT+C , then drag a rectangle over the area you want the zone to cover. Give the zone a name and choose whether it should be displayed, spoken, or both.

To trigger a reading zone, press CAPS LOCK+ALT+ the zone’s number (1 through 9, or 0 for zone 10). Press CAPS LOCK+ALT+N to move to the next zone and CAPS LOCK+ALT+P to move to the previous zone, or press CAPS LOCK+ALT+L to list all your zones.

For example, if you regularly check a dashboard with multiple widgets, set up Reading Zones for the most important ones. With a single keystroke, ZoomText can magnify or speak the data you need, without searching the page for it.

es.summary: Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación, la rc 1 de NVDA 2026.3 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Se recomienda a todos los usuarios descargar esta versión y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, o por el sistema de informe de fallos de NV Access. A menos … Continuar leyendo "Ya disponible la primera candidata a liberación de NVDA 2026.3" La entrada Ya disponible la primera candidata a liberación de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
es.body:
Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación , la rc 1 de NVDA 2026.3 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Se recomienda a todos los usuarios descargar esta versión y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, o por el sistema de informe de fallos de NV Access . A menos que se detecten fallos críticos de última hora, esta versión será idéntica a la versión final de NVDA 2026.3. Esta versión no es apta para entornos de producción. Al instalar esta rc te unirás al canal beta, y sólo recibirás avisos de actualización de compilaciones beta y candidatas a liberación (rc). El canal beta/rc siempre te mantendrá al día con la versión más reciente de NVDA. La última rc de un ciclo de liberación es idéntica a la última versión estable. Para regresar al canal de versiones estables, instala a mano la última versión estable.

Esta versión incorpora importantes mejoras de rendimiento, mejoras en los diálogos de NVDA, y entrada expandida por la pantalla táctil. Se han hecho varias mejoras para reducir los retrasos y aumentar el rendimiento. Ahora NVDA recupera y captura más información sobre los controles en segundo plano, mejorando el rendimiento en controles como cuadros combinados y el explorador de archivos. NVDA ya no hace que se rompan el explorador de archivos u otras aplicaciones al cerrarlo o reiniciarlo. NVDA se recupera ahora más rápido cuando una aplicación deja de responder, y ya no se colgará ni inundará el registro con errores en aplicaciones que no responden. En regiones vivas de texto, como las terminales, NVDA ya no se cuelga cuando se vuelcan en pantalla importantes cantidades de texto. Se han añadido menús de contexto y atajos de teclado a los diálogos de perfiles de configuración, gestos de entrada y diccionarios del habla, haciendo que estos diálogos sean más fáciles de usar con el teclado. Ahora también es posible cambiar directamente un gesto existente en el diálogo Gestos de entrada. Se ha modernizado el diálogo que presenta mensajes explorables y ahora soporta mejor cambiar su tamaño, maximizarlo y minimizarlo. Se ha expandido significativamente la entrada por pantalla táctil. Los gestos de dos deslizamientos secuenciales ahora combinan dos deslizamientos en rápida sucesión en un solo gesto, incrementando enormemente la cantidad de gestos asociables. También se soportan ahora los gestos de borde, permitiendo que los gestos que comiencen a 15 mm de cualquier borde de la pantalla se asocien independientemente de los mismos gestos realizados en el centro de la pantalla. Se ha añadido una nueva orden sin asignar para mover el cursor del ratón al centro de la vista ampliada. Se puede usar el OCR de Windows con la lupa o la cortina de pantalla activadas. Se ha actualizado Liblouis con nuevas tablas braille en Elfdaliano, sami, maorí, braille unificado inglés de Nueva Zelanda, y aitiano criollo, una tabla noruega para texto en español, y variantes adicionales de sueco de 6 y 8 puntos. Se ha actualizado Espeak NG añadiendo soporte para liguriano y abkhaz. Para instalar esta rc, puedes configurar el canal «rc y beta» en el complemento Selector del canal de actualización y buscar actualizaciones desde el menú Ayuda de NVDA, o actualizar desde una beta anterior. Y como siempre, también puedes descargar manualmente el instalador de NVDA 2026.3 rc 1 . Su suma de comprobación SHA256, que te permitirá garantizar la integridad del archivo descargado, es f233fe4c2134560c3b945e94ce4c1835a62c511fa22a64bdaa521289bedccc3d. ¡Feliz miércoles!

La entrada Ya disponible la primera candidata a liberación de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .

en.title: In-Process 16th October 2026
en.summary: We’ve got a bumper edition for you this week, with new content for just about everyone! Accessibility Testing with NVDA NV Access Survey New Help Options for NVDA Users Help for Low Vision Users Free Sample Accessibility Testing with NVDA NVDA 2026.3 Beta 5 Accessibility Testing with NVDA NV Access is very pleased to announce… Read More
en.body:
We’ve got a bumper edition for you this week, with new content for just about everyone!

NV Access is very pleased to announce the release of a new training package. Accessibility Testing with NVDA is designed for people using NVDA to test apps and websites for accessibility.

This Accessibility Testing with NVDA package includes: A training module with over 60 topics in nine sections Getting Started Setting up NVDA Reading information Visual Options Keyboard navigation Navigating content with NVDA Working with elements Testing with a screen reader Reporting Issues A printable NVDA Reference Sheet, with the commands most useful for accessibility testing A printable guide to writing accessible content on a single, printable sheet for easy consultation A list of NV Access and external resources and links to further your knowledge A WCAG 2.2 Reference with tips on testing many of the criteria with NVDA A JPG Badge you can proudly display in your email, or on your website or elsewhere to indicate your support

The purchase price of the module is A$250 (+GST for Australian buyers). Not only do you get a wealth of accessibility testing information, the cost of this package also supports the work of NV Access and helps continue our ability to provide the NVDA screen reading software free of charge.

Please note that this package is useable by both sighted and screen reader users. It is aimed at professionals wanting to test websites, documents and programs for accessibility. If you would like to learn to use NVDA from scratch as a blind or low vision screen reader user, please first consider “ Basic Training for NVDA ” or the “ NVDA Productivity Bundle “.

The Accessibility Testing with NVDA module is designed to teach you to incorporate NVDA into your accessibility testing workflow. It is not intended to replace dedicated accessibility testing tools which can give specific information about testing criteria and compliance etc. If you would like more formal training specifically in web accessibility, we recommend Learn.Intopia.digital . Intopia provided feedback on the web accessibility components of this material.

Please head to Accessibility Testing with NVDA to read more and purchase the new package.

Cover image of “Accessibility Testing with NVDA”

The NVDA Satisfaction Survey 2026 is open, but only until early next week.

We are always interested in understanding the satisfaction of our NVDA users, what is important to you & what we can do more effectively. The survey is anonymous & we encourage you to leave comments in your response.

We’re interested in hearing from as many people as possible, so please feel free to pass this on to others.

The survey is short, only three questions – we deliberately do that in order to make it less onerous to fill out. The rating is a simple, and industry standard metric (a “net promoter score”) we can use to benchmark broadly how well we are doing compared to previous years. We leave room for you to add your own thoughts, so you can give feedback on that one specific point on your mind. If you want a response, please do include your email address as we don’t otherwise collect contact details.

We do sometimes get questions like “It would be great if NVDA had feature X” and it’s frustrating to not be able to reply, especially when NVDA does in fact have feature X, but we have no way to reach the person to share that with them. We have also been asked “Why don’t you ask more questions about X, Y, or Z?” – which is a great question. This survey is designed to collect feedback on everything overall, and we try to keep it fairly consistent from year to year. We do conduct specific surveys from time to time, both more formally, and occasionally just a simple question on Mastodon asking, “What do you think about …”. We like to think we are approachable and easy to get in contact with, so do please always reach out if there is something you’d like to give feedback on or to ask.

Please do head over to https://www.nvaccess.org/survey2026 and fill out the survey if you haven’t already.

We are always looking for ways to help users and make more information available, and easy to find. For many years, the navbar of the NV Access website has had a “Get Help” option. This has linked to a single page of really useful information for NVDA users , including the training material, user groups, how to report an issue or get extra voices, and an FAQ. Now, we have expanded it to a menu. The first item lets you get help for “NVDA Users” and is the original “Get Help” item.

There are also several new options, which are covered below:

With the release of the magnifier in NVDA 2026.2, it seemed a good time to collate some of the features and settings in NVDA which can be useful for low vision users. The way low vision users will have NVDA setup may be different to how a totally blind user who does not use the screen may have it setup. This “ Get Help for Low Vision Users ” page includes information about: The magnifier: including a demo video, list of keystrokes, and link to the comparison with Windows Magnifier we did here in In-Process. Visual Highlighter: How to turn it on and just what the different colours mean. How to reduce speech: Turning on or off individual elements, or adjusting the speech mode overall. Working on the Web: Tips for navigating web pages, and copying information from the web. Other Windows Settings: Suggestions for other Windows settings which can be useful for low vision users.

To go with the brand-new Accessibility Testing with NVDA package , we have made a free sample of the material available. This extensive sample is full of web accessibility tips and tricks with the world’s favourite free screen reader, and is still only a small taste of the full product.

Do check out the Accessibility Testing with NVDA sample page in the new revamped “Get Help” menu. If you find it useful, you will find even more in the full Accessibility Testing with NVDA package , plus you will be supporting us to keep NVDA available for free to everyone who can use it.

Once again, our thanks to Intopia.Digital for their ongoing support of NV Access.

Finally, this week, we’re now up to Beta 5 of NVDA 2026.3 . Last In-Process we were up to Beta 2, so here’s what’s been in the latest three updates:

Changes introduced in Beta 5: Updates to translations Added bug fix for NVDA failing to start on Windows versions older than Windows 10 1903

Changes introduced in Beta 4: Updates to translations Added bug fix for lag in the Add-on Store when searching using Chinese characters Minor documentation changes

Changes introduced in Beta 3: Updates to translations Reverted bug fix to terminals, meaning NVDA may freeze again when substantial amounts of text are dumped to the screen. This is due to the bug fix not working correctly Prevented Magnifier crash recovery from flashing to reduce seizure risk

That’s all for this week. It’s not often the latest beta gets bumped to the SIXTH article in the blog! That by no means reflects on its value though – Please do try NVDA 2026.3 Beta 5 if you haven’t already. If you do any web accessibility work, please do check out the new Accessibility Testing with NVDA Package . It will be around release time for NVDA 2026.3 by next edition, so we’ll have more on the new version. And we’ll also cover a bit more for our low vision users as well.

en.title: From Word to Teams: Using ZoomText and Fusion Across Your Workday
en.summary: ZoomText and Fusion are powerful accessibility tools designed for people with low vision. ZoomText is a screen magnifier and reader, while Fusion combines all of ZoomText’s features with the full JAWS screen reader, offering both magnification and speech. Since October is National Disability Employment Awareness Month, we want to take this opportunity to spotlight powerful …
en.body:
ZoomText and Fusion are powerful accessibility tools designed for people with low vision. ZoomText is a screen magnifier and reader, while Fusion combines all of ZoomText’s features with the full JAWS screen reader, offering both magnification and speech.

Since October is National Disability Employment Awareness Month, we want to take this opportunity to spotlight powerful features of ZoomText and Fusion that will help you be more productive in the workplace. This blog series will run throughout October, with a new post every Thursday featuring helpful information and practical tips to make the most of ZoomText and Fusion as you work.

For many professionals, the workday is a journey through Microsoft Office and a variety of collaboration tools. Whether you’re writing, analyzing data, managing emails, or joining virtual meetings, having ZoomText or Fusion set up to support your workflow can make all the difference. This week, we’ll look at how these tools can help you work more efficiently and comfortably, from your first document to your last video call.

Drafting reports or editing proposals is easier when you can see exactly what you need. With ZoomText, you can quickly adjust your magnification level or switch between different zoom window types—like Lens or Line view—to focus on the text that matters most. For longer documents, AppReader is a helpful feature: just press CAPS LOCK+ALT+A to have the text read aloud, letting you follow along visually or simply listen and rest your eyes.

Fusion users can also take advantage of JAWS navigation commands, such as jumping between headings or moving by paragraph, to quickly scan and organize content. To jump by heading, first turn on Quick Navigation keys by pressing CAPS LOCK+Z , then press H to navigate forward through headings or SHIFT+H to navigate backward. Press P to navigate forward by paragraph and SHIFT+P to navigate backward. Press CAPS LOCK+Z to toggle Quick Navigation keys off again so you can continue editing your document.

Keyboard Echo is another useful feature, giving you spoken feedback as you type, so you can be sure your edits are accurate.

To cycle through the different Keyboard Echo settings, press CAPS LOCK+ALT+K . The setting No Echo disables all keyboard echo. Keys will echo your keystrokes as you type. Words will echo individual words as you type them. And Keys and Words will echo both keystrokes and words as you type.

Spreadsheets can be intimidating, but ZoomText’s magnification tools help you zero in on the data you need. Adjust your zoom to see more or less of your sheet and use Reading Zones to mark important areas—like totals or headers—so you can return to them instantly.

A reading zone is a defined area of an application window that ZoomText can display, speak, or both, at the press of a hotkey. To create a reading zone, press CAPS LOCK+ALT+C , then drag a rectangle over the area of the application window you want the zone to cover. To trigger a reading zone, press CAPS LOCK+ALT+ the zone’s number (1 through 9, or 0 for zone 10).

Fusion users can rely on JAWS table navigation to move efficiently through rows and columns, with commands like CAPS LOCK+C to read the current cell, helping you keep your place in complex data.

Staying on top of emails and appointments is simple with the right tools. AppReader lets you listen to long emails, while Focus Enhancements in ZoomText highlight your current selection, making it easier to track where you are.

AppReader reads documents, web pages, and email aloud while you follow along or rest your eyes. It can read from beginning to end, skim forward and backward, or read just the text you select with the mouse. AppReader reads text aloud in three modes: App View reads directly in the source application without changing your view, Text View reformats the text with your choice of fonts, colors, and magnification for easier reading, and the SpeakIt Tool reads any text on the screen that you select by clicking and dragging. Press CAPS LOCK+ALT+A to launch App View. Press CAPS LOCK+ALT+T to launch Text View. Press CAPS LOCK+ALT+S to launch the SpeakIt Tool.

Focus enhancements highlight the item you are on as you navigate using the Tab and arrow keys through menus, dialogs, and toolbars, making it easy to keep your place. Press CAPS LOCK+F to toggle focus enhancements on and off.

Fusion users can use commands like CTRL+N to create a new message, CTRL+R to reply to a message, or CTRL+F to forward a message. You can also switch to different areas in Outlook with quick shortcuts like CTRL+1 to go to your current mail folder, CTRL+2 to navigate to the calendar, and CTRL+3 to go to Contacts.

Whether you’re building slides or presenting to your team, ZoomText’s flexible magnification ensures you can see every detail. AppReader can read slide content aloud, making it easier to review your work or follow along during a presentation. Fusion users can use the arrow keys with JAWS to navigate slides and read speaker notes, so you’re always prepared and in control. Press F6 in PowerPoint to navigate the different areas of your presentation.

Today’s workplace relies on video conferencing apps like Microsoft Teams, Zoom, and Google Meet. With ZoomText and Fusion, you can adjust your magnification to follow chat messages, participant panels, and shared screens during meetings. AppReader and JAWS speech help you keep up with notifications and chat without missing a beat.

A standout feature for video calls is Face-in-View . Before joining a meeting, open the Face-in-View tool in Fusion by pressing INSERT+SPACE, F , then O . This feature uses your webcam to show you a live preview and provides feedback to help you center your face and check your lighting—so you can join every call looking your best and feeling confident.

Join us next week as we explore how ZoomText and Fusion can help you access more online, making web browsing and digital resources easier and more accessible. Stay tuned for more tips to help you thrive in your workplace!

Have questions? Email training@vispero.com .

With the right setup and a few helpful features, ZoomText and Fusion can empower you to work smarter and more comfortably, every step of the way.

en.title: Welcome Home: Apple Announces Updated HomePod Mini, Apple TV, All-New HomeView, and New Home Accessories
en.summary: Apple today announced updated models of the HomePod Mini and Apple TV 4K ; as well as an all-new HomeView smart home hub and a collection of smart home accessories . HomePod Mini 2 Powered by the S10 chip and what Apple calls "advanced computational audio," up to four HomePod Mini 2 or HomePod (2nd generation) speakers can be paired to create a surround sound experience with the new Apple TV 4K. Siri AI will be available on HomePod Mini 2 with a future software update. It can recognize up to six people in a household, and can use a user's Apple Intelligence-capable iPhone or iPad to draw on their personal context. With Sound Glow, the top of HomePod Mini 2 can glow and pulse in sync with the currently playing song. Users can additionally customize the displayed animations to promote a relaxing atmosphere. HomePod Mini 2 features 100 percent recycled rare earth elements in all magnets, and 100 percent recycled copper, gold plating, and tin solder in all Apple-designed circuit boards. It can be pre-ordered from Apple starting today in pink, green, blue, white and midnight for US $149, and will begin shipping to customers on Friday, October 30. HomeView HomeView is a smart home hub with a speaker and 7-inch display, which can either be placed on a table or mounted on a wall. It features a variety of Apple apps and widgets on the Home Screen, and allows users to play music, view photos and videos, make and receive FaceTime calls, monitor and control their home, and more using Siri or the touch interface. HomeView can display a generic screen for everyone in the household, or recognize up to six faces to show personalized content for individual users. Apple Silicon and HomeView's speaker array can optimize audio for loudness and bass response at any volume, with tailored profiles for the table-top and wall-mounted models. Siri AI can be used to play media on HomeView, answer general knowledge questions, discuss recipes, and if a user has an Apple Intelligence-capable iPhone or iPad, draw on their personal context for more helpful responses. Like other Apple Intelligence-capable devices, conversations with Siri AI on HomeView are synced via iCloud and viewable in the Siri app on iOS, iPadOS, and macOS. Changes made to Siri's pace or expressiveness on compatible devices are synced to HomeView. HomeView features a wide variety of watchOS-style faces that can display snippets of information at a glance, a user's photos, or interactive art. With a supported iCloud+ subscription, HomeView can integrate with compatible cameras to recognize people, pets, packages, and vehicles, and can describe captured video using AI. With Sound Recognition, HomeView can alert users to smoke and carbon monoxide detectors on their iPhone, iPad, or Apple Watch. Similar to the security and privacy features of other Apple products, data processed by the A18 chip's Secure Exclaves is isolated from the HomeView software and does not leave the device. Users' personal content, like messages and calendar, is only displayed when the user's face is recognized and their iPhone or iPad is present and has been recently unlocked. The wall-mounted HomeView model can optionally be professionally installed. HomeView is made with 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure base and in the enclosure of the wall-mounted model, 100 percent gold plating and tin solder in all Apple-designed circuit boards, and 100 percent recycled rare earth elements in all magnets. It can be pre-ordered from Apple starting today for US $299, and will begin shipping to customers on Friday, November 13. The table-top model is available in silver, starlight, rose pink, and space gray finishes, with the wall-mounted model available in space gray and silver finishes. Apple TV 4K With the A19 chip, Apple claims the new Apple TV 4K delivers up to 50 percent faster CPU performance and up to 2X faster GPU performance when compared to the previous generation. In addition, a new, dedicated AV1 decoder enables more efficient streaming while using less bandwidth. Continuing on the theme of recent Apple product unveilings, the new Apple TV 4K supports Siri AI for smarter voice interactions. Users can find entertainment and control their smart home with more flexible natural language, and Siri AI's awareness of personal context and onscreen content can be used to answer questions about home events or what's currently playing. Users with an Apple Intelligence-capable iPhone or iPad will be able to use Siri AI on Apple TV 4K (2nd and 3rd generation). Three far-field microphones on the new Apple TV 4K support Siri hands-free, allowing users to prompt it by saying "Siri" or "Hey Siri," as they do on other Apple devices. The new Siri Remote supports Find My with Precision Finding, which can guide users to the remote's precise location, useful if it, for example, falls between couch cushions. Like other Find My-capable devices, the remote can also play a sound to help users locate it. Similar to other Apple products, data processed by the Secure Exclaves is isolated from tvOS and does not leave the device. The new Apple TV 4K features 100 percent recycled gold plating and tin solder in all Apple-designed circuit boards, and 100 percent recycled rare earth elements in all magnets. It can be pre-ordered from Apple starting today for US $299, and will begin shipping to customers on Friday, November 13. Home Collection In collaboration with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric, Apple has launched a collection of smart home accessories, including a lock, doorbell, thermostats, temperature sensors, and indoor and outdoor cameras. These accessories support NFC for one-tap setup on iPhone, and will begin rolling out in December.

en.title: Getting Started: Essential ZoomText and Fusion Features for the Workplace
en.summary: ZoomText and Fusion are powerful accessibility tools designed for people with low vision.
